product-double-wall-frame-tray-sleeve.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Double-Wall Frame Tray and Sleeve Sourcing

Review a double wall frame tray and sleeve throughout the sliding route, not only at the closed position. Show the frame perimeter, loaded product height and sleeve seam on the proposal. A tray that fits once seated may still contact an edge or seam while entering or leaving the sleeve.

The frame tray and enclosing sleeve are separate components with a moving interface. Their material, fold and seam details belong on the same sample record. A closed beauty view conceals most of that interface.

Draw the frame perimeter and sleeve interior

The frame tray and sleeve reference identifies a double-wall frame tray paired with a sleeve. Ask for the proposed drawing to show which perimeter parts travel nearest the sleeve walls and where its seam lies.

Label the tray's outside envelope separately from the visible frame opening. Add the highest point of the complete contents. Keep the sleeve inside dimensions and prepared seam on a second component view.

Compare the frame tray and lid direction when a lift-off action suits the pack better. The extra requirement here is clearance during movement rather than just paired closure.

Run entry and removal with the frame loaded

Form the double walls and frame as proposed, then load the actual holder and product. Insert the tray along the intended direction. Pause at entry, midway and the final closed position.

For a hypothetical ornament gift, the frame may surround a product that stands slightly proud of the opening. Record that loaded height and view its route past the sleeve edge. An empty tray trial would leave that question unanswered.

Keep the sleeve in a consistent position during comparison. If the reviewer squeezes it or rotates the tray to get past a contact, record that action. Don't treat the adjusted maneuver as evidence that the intended route works.

Use a travel contact map

Assign contact locations on a simple perimeter sketch. Each observation should include the travel stage and which component touches.

Travel stageArea to inspectRecord
EntryLeading frame edge and sleeve mouthInitial alignment and first contact
MidwayFrame sides and internal seamLocation of rubbing or obstruction
ClosedLoaded height and end positionSeated envelope and available grip
RemovalTrailing edge and product heightExit contact and customer action

A contact at the mouth and a contact along a seam are different issues. Send separate marked photographs so the supplier can compare them with the construction drawing.

Agree supplied preparation and the opening end

State how tray and sleeve arrive and who forms each. Request a view of prepared double-wall folds and the sleeve seam. Confirm whether either end is closed and how the customer begins removal.

Review the final proposed board, caliper, print and surface finish after the route is defined. If those details change, reopen the movement check. A material name without a sample revision cannot establish the same interface.

Inspect the frame and sleeve surfaces after the agreed actions. Record visible contact marks as sample observations. This method doesn't quantify wear life, friction or protective performance; any required evaluation needs its own scope.

Mark which frame edge leads during entry. A tray may look symmetrical from above while its folds or product arrangement differ at the two ends. Reversing it during a trial changes the travel map. If both directions are permitted, keep two records with their respective leading edges and compare the same stages.

product-double-wall-tray-lid.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Double-Wall Tray and Lid Sourcing

Specify a double-wall tray-and-lid set through its wall section and usable cavity. Identify the panels that form the full doubled walls, then review the separate lid over the loaded tray. Compare that section with a hollow frame return and with a simpler folding lid/base set before fixing the insert layout.

This concept explains a doubled-wall interface; the actual wall preparation, board and lid fit are confirmed on the offered drawing.

Draw the wall section as well as the outside shape

The double-wall tray-and-lid reference identifies the named set. Esko’s ArtiosCAD tray catalogue includes double-sidewall/double-endwall drawings. Ask the converter for its own section through the inner wall, outer wall and corner joint, plus a formed tray view.

Record which panels are factory prepared and which are folded at packing. A catalogue name does not establish that every wall is glued, locked or erected in the same order. Show those operations individually and attach the supplied-state description to the component IDs.

Locate the usable cavity after the wall returns are formed. Include the insert, finished gift and card in that space. An outside length and width cannot explain how much room is occupied by a returned wall or whether an insert sits over it.

Compare full walls with a frame return

The double-wall frame tray-and-lid direction introduces a raised frame or hollow rim around the product. A frame-tray construction description identifies inward-folded walls forming that rim. Compare the section, cavity edge and lid engagement rather than deciding by similar product names.

The folding lid-and-base set is another alternative with two separately formed pieces. Hold the gift contents constant while comparing the wall formation, lid placement and customer removal. The useful output is a description of different actions and clearances, not an unsupported ranking of strength.

Seat the proposed lid over a fully loaded tray and inspect its contact with the formed walls. Remove the lid through the intended grip, then remove the gift. If a wall return lifts with an insert or a card sits in the lid engagement area, locate that interface and ask for the next revision.

Use a wall-section comparison record

The hypothetical entries distinguish tray construction from decorative finish.

Comparison fieldFull doubled-wall proposalQuestion to resolve
Wall sectionInner and outer wall panels labeled W1/W2Which joints are prepared or formed locally?
Cavity edgeInsert I1 seats inside formed wallsDoes any return overlap the insert?
Lid engagementSeparate lid L1 over tray T1Where does the loaded lid contact?
Frame alternativeRaised rim shown in a separate sectionHow does the usable cavity change?
RemovalLid lift followed by product gripDoes another component move with it?

Ask for the section that settles the comparison

The converter should return wall and lid sections with component revisions. The packing owner should verify that the described delivered pieces can be formed in the planned order. The buyer can then compare complete sample states using the same contents and decide which cavity and opening route to develop.

product-drawstring-fabric-gift-bag.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Drawstring Fabric Gift Bag Sourcing

Specify a drawstring fabric gift bag through its usable opening, sewn channel and cord exit positions. Review the gathered closure above the actual primary pack, then reopen it through the intended grip. A flat bag size alone does not show the loading mouth or the space occupied by the closed neck.

This is an AI-assisted concept direction for a drawstring construction. The offered fabric, cord and channel details require supplier confirmation.

Separate the flat bag from its open mouth

The original fabric pouch and bag reference lists drawstring among available closure types. A fabric converter leaflet also identifies cord and ribbon fastening options. Use those as closure vocabulary, then request the actual channel and exit drawing for the proposed bag.

Supply the finished primary-pack envelope, including corners and any decoration. State whether the bag receives a small jewelry box, a wrapped component or a boxed gift. Record the opening as a usable loading space, separate from the flat seam-to-seam dimensions.

Mark where the cord leaves the channel and how far the gathered neck sits above the contents. Identify any stopper, knot or other offered termination. The choice affects the closing and release action and should stay connected to the bag drawing.

Review gathering around the packed shape

Load through the open mouth using the intended orientation. Photograph the corners passing the channel and any handle or cord obstruction. Gather the bag through the offered cord route, then check the neck relative to the contents and printed identity.

Open it again using the planned customer grip. Record a corner snag, cord crossing or need to press against the product at its actual location. Ask for a revised opening/channel proposal or a confirmed loading action rather than treating the difficulty as a general fabric question.

Compare the existing textile jewelry pouch for the broad holder choice. The zippered fabric pouch adds a slider and end-stop opening instead. Keep the same primary pack in the comparison so the distinct closure routes can be reviewed.

Use an opening and gathering record

These hypothetical jewelry-box entries leave the actual fabric and cord proposals open.

Bag interfaceExample inputReview evidence
Usable mouthJewelry box in finished packagingLoading view at its widest corners
Channel C1Sewn channel and cord entry/exit mapOffered construction detail
Cord endsTermination and customer grip proposalGathered and reopened states
Closed neckSpace above box lid and decorationComplete closed bag view
Product contactBox finish and prohibited snag areaLocated loading/removal observation

Assign the remaining closure questions

The fabric converter should identify the channel, cord and seam proposal. The packing owner should show the actual loading and gathering sequence. The buyer should review the closed presentation and customer reopening together, with any corner clearance question still linked to the same primary-pack dimensions.

Use the gift bag and tissue direction if a carried boxed gift needs another opening/handle arrangement. Send the usable mouth, channel map and gathered-neck question through Get a Quote. MOQ is 500 pieces per design; materials, samples and commercial details are confirmed for the project.

Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Paper Gift Carrier Sourcing

Plan a paper gift carrier from the complete boxed gift, usable loading mouth, gusset and handle construction. Compare euro-tote and wide-gusset proposals while keeping their actual folds and handle attachments identified.

Compare the loading mouth, expanded gusset and handle route

A wide gusset describes the proposed carrier geometry, not a handle specification or proof that it matches a particular euro-tote construction. Review the complete boxed gift during entry as well as after the sides expand.

RelationshipWhat to identifySample question
Entry through the mouthClosed gift-box envelope, added wrap, tag or tissue, entry orientation and the usable opening.Can the complete gift enter without an unplanned change to the box or presentation?
Expanded side foldsActual gusset folds, formed interior, base and final position of the gift.Where do the box corners, tissue and folded bag surfaces meet after loading?
Handle accessHandle type, attachment, reinforcement and the highest packed component.Is the intended grip and removal route available with the full gift present?

Show the entry and final loaded orientations separately when they differ. An outside width or an empty upright bag does not establish the expanded usable space. Ask for the offered bag drawing, actual handle joints and delivery state instead of carrying dimensions from a different carrier.

Keep material, base construction and any carrying evaluation tied to the selected proposal. A larger gusset does not by itself establish a higher carrying capacity.

This enquiry direction needs confirmation of actual paper, construction and delivered form. Treat any reinforcement, carry use and decorative finish as proposed features to review.

Request inside and outside handle views

The euro tote catalogue names the carrier direction and includes handle options. Ask the supplier to identify the actual handle material and attachment method for your proposal. Keep hidden joining work distinct from the outside appearance.

Show each handle join and any top reinforcement on an inside view. Include the proposed base construction separately. A matching handle color does not establish a matching attachment or material.

Ask which parts arrive assembled and which work remains at packing. A complete carrier and a bag with separately supplied handle components describe different delivery scopes.

Review the gift around the grip route

Provide the finished gift-box envelope, actual weight and all tissue or cards. Show the box orientation within the gusset. Mark the height of any component near the handles.

For a hypothetical boxed ornament, tissue may stand above the gift box. Review whether that complete arrangement leaves the intended hand grip clear. Record any rearrangement needed before the handoff.

Remove the gift after the carry-position review. A wide opening in an empty bag can become a different access route when handles, folded top areas and the gift are present together.

Use a handle-interface sheet

Keep the supplied construction and loaded sample identity with each observation. The sheet should not contain an invented capacity.

InterfaceProposal detailSample question
Handle outsideMaterial and visible gripCan the hand use the intended route?
Handle insideAttachment and covering layersWhich joint belongs to the proposal?
Top reinforcementLocation and component identityDoes it meet the opening or contents?
BaseFold or support proposalWhere does the gift sit?
Loaded accessFull contents and gussetCan gift and tissue be removed as planned?

The gift bag and tissue set page considers the complete presentation. This sheet adds the construction interfaces behind its carrier choice.

Compare a specific handoff requirement

In the hypothetical record, call the handle H1, its join J1 and the full gift configuration G1. Ask for J1 on the actual sample rather than accepting a generic handle swatch. Keep G1 present for the grip review.

If the supplier proposes a different top reinforcement, identify that component revision and repeat the loaded opening check. A changed hidden layer can reopen access while leaving the outside artwork nearly identical.

Any carrying-capacity or repeated-use requirement needs a responsible evaluation with the actual load and conditions. The local sheet records parts, fit and action; it does not convert a short observation into a performance guarantee.

Bring the hidden construction to the enquiry

Home / Inserts
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Through-Cut EVA Insert Sourcing

A through-cut EVA insert needs the cut top layer and its separate backing identified as two components. Review the cavity edge and finger recess against the actual product before accepting removal access. Keep the grade, thickness and attachment proposals with this layer construction rather than treating EVA as a complete holder specification.

This concept shows a through-cut top piece and backing. The offered EVA grade, layers and attachment are confirmed for the project.

Give the top and backing separate identities

The original Evazote grade information identifies a closed-cell copolymer block-foam grade and compression-related fields. It demonstrates the need for an actual grade reference; its typical values are guidance for that grade, not Packrivo holder specifications.

Ask for the offered top-layer cavity outline and backing/attachment BOM, including the proposed cutting and joining method. Mark whether a separate backing or another agreed support completes the cavity. These are project-specific supplier proposals.

Supply the finished product, primary wrap and intended contact restrictions. Identify which surface approaches the exposed cut wall during insertion and lift. Keep the finger recess on the top-layer drawing so its position can be reviewed alongside the product grip.

Compare the through-cut interface with a depth-cut bed

The contour-cut PU bed retains material beneath a depth-cut pocket. This EVA configuration instead exposes a through-cut wall above a separately identified backing. Hold the product arrangement constant while comparing the layer, contact and removal questions.

Load the actual product, check its seating on the backing and review the lift through the intended recess. Inspect the cut-wall contact and any movement between the offered layers. Retain the grade and sample identity with the agreed observation method.

If the converter changes the backing, attachment or recess, record the affected component and drawing revision. A proposed grade change should remain a separate field so the buyer can distinguish material identity from a changed cavity geometry.

Use a cut-layer and backing table

The hypothetical jewelry-holder entries below make the separate components visible.

InterfaceExample brief inputNext evidence
Top layer T1Through-cut cavity and proposed thicknessActual outline/section
Backing B1Separate component and attachment proposalLayer BOM and seated product
Cut edge E1Finished product/contact restrictionLocated insertion/removal observation
Finger recess G1Proposed grip beside the cavityActual product lift route
Grade F1Supplier grade and technical referenceMaterial/compression proposal kept separate

Keep layer changes in the review record

The foam converter confirms the offered top, backing and attachment construction. The buyer supplies the actual finish restrictions. The packing observer returns the loaded and removal states, and the buyer decides whether another cavity or layer proposal is needed.

Use the die-cut insert direction and the inserts hub for the broader holder comparison. The insert-material guide keeps actual grade questions visible without turning them into a protection guarantee.

product-expandable-kraft-parcel-bag.post_title: Custom Expandable Kraft Parcel Bag Sourcing
product-expandable-kraft-parcel-bag.post_content:
Home / Mailer Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Expandable Kraft Parcel Bag Sourcing

Review an expandable kraft parcel bag at two named complete fills and record closing reach at each. Show the gusset proposal, highest packed point and final closing area. Extra space in a concept doesn't establish that the flap can meet its intended seal when the actual contents expand the bag.

Treat this as an enquiry direction until the supplier confirms the material, side folds, seam and closure for the project.

Define fills instead of an unlimited size range

The expandable kraft mailer reference describes an expandable form and asks for gusset depth. Request the actual folded and expanded geometry for your proposal. Keep the usable filled envelope separate from flat outside dimensions.

Name the thinner and thicker contents sets. Include all wrapping and backing components in each. Record where the highest point sits so the comparison doesn't reduce a shaped bundle to one thickness number.

For a hypothetical gift-print order, one fill may contain cards and another cards plus a booklet. Keep their contents lists and orientations distinct throughout the closing review.

Check closure after the folds expand

Load the actual bundle and form the gussets as proposed. Observe the closing flap before pressing or joining it. Ask the supplier to identify the intended receiving area and closing method.

Compare that reach at both fills. If staff need to change a fold position or compress the contents, record the action and confirm whether it belongs in the instruction. A closed photo alone can conceal the change.

The general paper mailer direction is useful for the wider outer-pack brief. This configuration adds the expanded-fill relationship to the closing surface.

Use an expanded-fill record

Keep one bag proposal revision and named contents identities in the table. Add dimensions only from the actual drawing or recorded measurement.

RelationshipThin fillThick fill
ContentsComplete components and orientationComplete additions and orientation
GussetFinal side-fold positionFinal side-fold position
Closing reachFlap against proposed receiving areaFlap against proposed receiving area
Outside label areaUsable final surfaceUsable final surface
Customer openingGrip and access routeGrip and access route

A missing closing reach is a configuration issue to discuss, not an invitation to invent a stronger adhesive. Ask which geometry or method the supplier proposes to change.

Record supplied state and complete-pack requirements

Confirm which seams and closure parts arrive prepared. Identify who opens the gussets, loads the parcel and closes it. Keep the proposed shipping-label surface separate from the decorative artwork face.

In the hypothetical record, call the thicker fill F2 and its closing observation CR2. A response about F1 doesn't close CR2. Review the revised proposal with F2 in the same orientation before changing its status.

The local record concerns fit and closure action. A protection or distribution requirement needs a separate evaluation of the complete system, with contents, handling route and responsible evidence identified.

Send both filled states

Custom Folding Gift Box with Decorative Finish Sourcing

MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design. Plan the quantity for each design in your brief.

Plan the formed gift box first, then specify the finish, its location and the reference against which you want to review it.

Concept direction · Feasibility unverified

Your starting brief

Send the packed gift dimensions, box opening and assembly preference with the artwork area and intended finish effect. Name the surfaces that need matching and the folds, edges or closure areas the finish must pass across.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

Separate structure from the finish request

  • Define the formed interior and all gift contents, including any insert, tissue, ribbon or card.
  • Mark the finish area on the current drawing, with the artwork version and the visual reference to compare.
  • Describe the packing and opening steps, including where the finished surface may fold or contact another component.

Choose the effect after the structure is clear

Printed color, a reflective foil effect and a raised or recessed detail call for different supplier proposals. Describe the effect you want rather than treating a concept image as a finish specification. Compare candidates on the selected construction and material; keep a simpler printed direction open if it answers the same presentation need.

If the finished box is part of a gift bag and tissue set, include those components separately in the scope. Use the gift bag and tissue checklist to keep their sizes, quantities and presentation requirements visible.

Review the finish on the formed candidate

  • Review the agreed finish under the same light and background as the reference; identify the surfaces included in the decision.
  • Form, close and open the complete box. Record any visible change at the scored folds, edges or closure contact points.
  • Keep the box drawing, artwork and reviewed physical sample together. A surface approval should name the part and finish it covers.

MOQ and project scope

MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design. State the quantity for each design, not just the combined order total. Packrivo helps organize the brief and supplier questions. The relevant supplier confirms the proposed materials, construction, price, sample scope and delivery timing for the agreed configuration.

Include your destination and any open inputs. If a detail is not yet known, name who will provide it before the next review.

Before you send a brief

Can I use my own branding?

Include your desired logo placement, print surfaces and colors. Final artwork must use the approved supplier dieline and pass proof review.

Can you make exactly what the picture shows?

The picture is an AI-assisted concept, not a production promise. Structure, materials, tolerances and finishing need supplier review and a physical sample.

What happens after an inquiry?

A person reviews the brief and missing details. Supplier checks and sample or quotation discussions follow only after the next steps are agreed.

Home / Mailer Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom FEFCO 0410 Five-Panel Corrugated Folder Sourcing

Use a FEFCO 0410 five-panel corrugated folder when a defined wrap sequence around the complete pack is the purchasing question. Identify the side, bottom, second side, lid and closing lip on the offered drawing. Review the end-flap order and final overlap around the actual gift rather than assuming every one-piece folder adjusts in the same way.

The illustration is an original concept based on the referenced geometry; the converter confirms the actual corrugated blank and closure proposal.

Follow the five body panels around the pack

The official FEFCO Code, 12th edition shows 0410 on page 48. Its body panel sequence includes side, bottom, side, lid and a closing lip, with end flaps. That drawing is a structural reference, not a Packrivo production drawing or a performance test.

Give those five panels local IDs on the offered proposal. Mark where the complete contents sit on the bottom panel and which side rises first. Include the thickest point of a boxed gift, primary wrap or card stack. Local projections can change the closing-lip question even when the main footprint is unchanged.

Ask for the end-flap sequence and the proposed final seal. Identify whether an adhesive, tape or another confirmed operation completes closure. The five-panel name alone does not supply that operation, its material or its owner.

Compare a fixed wrap with other folder tasks

The book-wrap corrugated pack may raise a different thickness/fold relationship, while the self-locking corrugated folder centers on an offered locking route. Keep these questions separate from the 0410 panel sequence instead of treating one-piece as the deciding feature.

Place the complete hypothetical gift pack on the starting panel and follow the offered order. Stop before end-flap and closing-lip operations to photograph the contents and overlap. Reopen along the intended customer route. Record the point where a tab, flap or sealed edge needs a different action; do not claim variable height unless the actual design provides it.

Use a panel and overlap record

For an illustrative gift print set, replace these IDs with the converter’s drawing labels.

Panel or closureExample inputEvidence to return
Bottom B1Backing board and print stack in final orientationStarting contents view
Sides S1/S2Offered side panel heightsPartly wrapped envelope
Lid L1Face alignment over the complete stackLoaded lid position

End flaps E1/E2Confirmed order beside the print edgesFolded end/contact view

Name the final closing owner

The converter should provide the revised blank and corrugated proposal. The packing owner should confirm who completes the end folds and final seal from the delivered state. The buyer should retain the reopened sample evidence and any distribution question for the completed configuration. The structural reference does not decide those responsibilities.

Compare the existing front-tuck mailer if a preformed cavity and loading step is preferable. The delivery-scope guide records the final packing operations.

PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Five-Panel Hanger Carton Sourcing

Specify a five panel hanger carton by separating the projecting hanger panel from the box body and end closures. Provide the real retail fixture and packed product weight. Check hanging presentation, lifting the carton off the fixture and opening the contents as three separate sample actions.

The hanger panel has a different job from an end flap. Keep its fold, hole and visible copy outside the assumptions used for a standard carton brief. Confirm the actual construction on a supplier drawing.

Identify the projecting fifth panel

PakFactory's five panel hanger reference identifies a carton intended for a hook or peg. That establishes the display direction; it doesn't verify a hanging capacity for your chosen product and material.

Show the box body, hanger fold and hole on a formed view. State whether the panel remains raised or folds down at another stage. Ask how it relates to the top closure so staff don't mistake one panel for the other.

Compare the existing tuck-end carton for the body and end-opening requirements. This configuration adds the fixture interface and the sequence of taking the pack off display.

Bring the actual fixture into the review

Provide the peg or hook shape, its usable length and any retaining feature. Include shelf or neighbouring-pack clearance that affects lifting the carton off. A generic circular hole in artwork is not a fixture specification.

For a hypothetical packaged key charm, weigh the complete pack with its card holder. Review it hanging in the intended orientation, then lift it off the peg without bending the panel as a shortcut.

Identify the expected display conditions and duration as requirements. Ask the responsible supplier what evaluation is appropriate. A brief sample observation should not be described as proof that the panel supports an unspecified weight for an unspecified time.

Separate three customer actions

Record the panel and closure positions during each action. Keep the same packed product in place.

ActionReference inputSample observation
Present on fixtureActual peg and packed weightFront orientation and hanger position
Lift off fixtureClearance above and around pegGrip and exit route
Open cartonIntended end and closureHanger panel clear of opening action
Remove productHolder and product envelopeFinger route and card orientation

If a hanger panel covers the opening instruction after removal, move the instruction in the artwork proposal. The information should be available when the customer needs it.

Confirm supplied state and forming

Ask whether the carton arrives flat, with a prepared side seam or in another agreed state. Include who raises the hanger panel, loads the contents and completes the ends. A display-ready supply scope should name those operations.

Inspect the hanger fold, hole edge and carton closures after the agreed sample actions. Record visible changes by location. If the hole shape or board changes, repeat fixture fit rather than carrying approval from the previous version.

Artwork should be checked with the hanger raised and in any later folded state. Keep the print face clear of the fixture where visibility matters. Materials, closure use and outer distribution packaging remain separate questions.

If multiple packs are intended to share one fixture, provide the arrangement as a requirement. Review removal from the intended position without assuming an isolated pack photograph represents it. The hanger panel's artwork and the customer's grip may meet neighbouring packs. Keep that observation separate from any future hanging-capacity assessment.

Send the fixture and opening brief together

Your starting brief

Send the packed product dimensions, proposed formed interior and closure, then identify the delivery state, assembly location and person responsible for final packing. Include the insert or divider in that scope.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

Define the two states of the mailer

  • List the dimensions and weight of the complete contents and the proposed formed box interior.
  • Ask the supplier to identify the flat delivery state, including the parts supplied and any separate fastening components.
  • Name who forms the box, fits the insert, loads the product and closes the completed package.

Compare flat and assembled scope

A flat-delivered proposal and an assembled proposal should identify the work still left to the buyer. Compare the same contents, closure and final configuration. Keep the assembly instructions and packing responsibilities with each response so a price difference is not mistaken for an equivalent scope.

Use the flat and assembled delivery worksheet to assign the remaining work before comparing the two delivery proposals.

  • Start with the candidate as supplied and follow the proposed assembly instructions; record any missing or ambiguous step.

Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Flip-Out Dispenser Carton Sourcing

Plan a flip out dispenser carton around the opening panel's travel and the customer's access to the units inside. Review the first, middle and last item in the proposed layout. A convenient-looking open panel doesn't confirm that the remaining contents can be reached or refilled without changing the arrangement.

This is an enquiry direction for repeated access through a defined opening. It needs a product count, unit orientation and refill decision. Keep those details separate from any assumption that contents feed themselves towards the opening.

Draw the panel in closed and open positions

PakFactory's flip out dispenser reference identifies a carton that flips open for access. Ask for the specific panel, hinge and limit of movement on your proposal. The named direction doesn't establish a universal dispensing mechanism.

Mark which part moves and which walls stay fixed. Specify where the panel should stop or rest, then ask the supplier to show the proposed support or restraint on the drawing. Include the space in front of the carton so the open panel isn't drawn through a shelf edge or neighbouring pack.

A display tray leaves its access area open. Compare the four corner display tray when that simpler action suits the product. The extra job here is controlling access through a moving panel.

Define how the units are presented inside

Provide the complete unit envelope, count and orientation. If the units are stacked, record which face points towards the opening. Include any divider or inner holder that changes the route.

For a hypothetical pack of individually wrapped gift cards, the opening might reveal the leading edge of a stack. Try taking one card without pulling the next card along. Repeat with a smaller stack, then with the final card in its intended position.

State whether staff move the contents forwards during use. A concept that needs that action should show it in the instruction. Don't describe the carton as automatic or self-feeding without a verified mechanism and appropriate evidence.

Keep a dispensing state record

Make a starting-state photo before each action. The rows distinguish panel movement from access to the changing contents.

StateActionEvidence
ClosedBegin panel openingStarting grip and hinge route
FullRemove first unitPanel position and neighbouring units
ReducedRemove a middle-stage unitReach and any manual rearrangement
Last itemRemove final unitGrip route without shaking carton
RefillAdd the next contents batchEntry point and reset position

If a unit sits beyond finger reach, record its exact position before moving it. That gives the supplier a concrete question about the opening, holder or internal arrangement.

Review supply and forming before use

Confirm the delivered state, prepared seams and setup sequence. Ask whether the access panel is pre-formed or needs an operator action. Identify who loads the initial contents and who refills later.

On the proposed material sample, inspect the moving fold and panel edges after the planned access actions. Record visible changes without assigning an unsupported cycle life. Any performance requirement needs an agreed evaluation scope.

Also check the print face in closed and open states. A message on the moving panel may face downwards or be hidden during use. Approve artwork against the formed views rather than a single front rendering.

If the remaining contents need manual repositioning, identify who does it and through which opening. Photograph that reset action as a separate state. The customer may use the front access panel while staff refill from another end. Naming both routes avoids asking one opening to perform two different jobs without a defined proposal.

Send the access sequence to Packrivo

Home / Inserts
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Flocked Foam Holder Sourcing

A flocked foam holder needs its base foam, adhesive/flock layer and exposed cut edges identified in the BOM. Review where the surface layer ends beside the cavity and where the actual product touches during removal. The visible textile-like face should not hide a different construction at the cut wall.

The concept illustrates a layered holder. Actual base grade, flock construction and cavity interfaces are confirmed for the project.

Name the layer on each actual face

Request a description of the proposed flocked surface, foam base, cut edges and any joining layers. Record which face would contact the actual gift and which surface remains exposed. A proposed layer description does not establish scratch resistance or the behavior of a finished gift on the offered holder.

Request the base foam grade, thickness and actual flock/adhesive construction. Mark which faces carry the layer and which cavity walls or edges remain exposed. Keep any lining, backing or attachment component in the same BOM.

Supply the actual product finish and permitted contact areas. Locate the intended removal grip beside the flock termination and cut edge. A top view of a covered face cannot show all the interfaces the product passes during loading or lift.

Review the layer termination at the product route

Load the actual product and observe its path into and out of the cavity. Inspect the exposed cut wall and the point where the layer ends. Record visible fibers, marks or another observation with its location, sample identity and conditions; retain any cause or performance question separately.

Compare the depth-cut PU bed or through-cut EVA holder through their own offered interfaces. A flocked-face proposal adds layer/BOM and termination questions; its base material remains a named supplier proposal rather than automatically EVA.

If the converter proposes a changed layer, edge or grip, keep that change attached to the earlier observation. Review the same finished product or explicitly name a substitute. The buyer needs to see which surface construction was actually compared.

Use a face, layer and cut-edge record

This original hypothetical jewelry-holder table distinguishes visible faces from exposed interfaces.

Surface/interfaceExample inputEvidence to return
Base F1Actual proposed foam grade and thicknessCurrent grade/BOM reference
Layer L1Flock/adhesive on named upper facesSupplier layer and face map
Termination E1Edge beside the product cavityActual section and close-up
Cut wall C1Exposed base or offered edge treatmentLocated product-contact observation
Grip G1Intended lift beside E1/C1Actual loading/removal sequence

Keep the surface question with the holder choice

The converter identifies the layer and exposed edges. The buyer supplies finish restrictions, while the packing observer returns located handling evidence. The buyer then decides whether the termination, contact or grip needs another proposed construction.

Use the current die-cut holder direction, inserts hub and material decision method as the real internal route. The sample revision record links any changed layer to its actual evidence.

product-flower-petal-top-gift-carton.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Flower Petal Top Gift Carton Sourcing

Specify a flower-petal top gift carton by its interlocking petal sequence, last-petal entry and customer opening touchpoint. Review the moving top panels above the complete product, with the bottom preparation recorded separately. This closure folds around an overlapping flower or rosette pattern rather than using an ordinary roll-end lid and dust flaps.

This concept direction requires supplier confirmation of the offered petal geometry, board, base and supplied state. The illustration explains the closure sequence.

Identify the petals and the final entry

PakFactory’s flower-petal top reference identifies folding-carton flaps that interlock into a flower-shaped top. A rosette-top carton description identifies a sequentially folded petal closure, separate tuck bottom and flat delivery with a prepared side seam. Those are narrow construction examples, not universal dimensions or Packrivo manufacturing claims.

Ask the converter to label every petal, its crease and the edge it overlaps. Mark which petal moves first and where the final one enters the offered overlap. Keep the actual panel count on the drawing rather than inferring it from the style name.

Supply the complete product and holder envelope. Identify the highest local projection beneath the moving top. A gift can sit inside the carton yet approach a petal as that panel crosses the opening. Record that movement with the product state and offered drawing.

Separate bottom setup from petal closing

Request the actual base construction and delivered preparation. State who forms the bottom before loading, which joints arrive prepared and what remains for local packing. The petal-top choice does not settle the bottom operation.

Compare the paperboard roll-end dust-flap carton directly. That direction forms rolled walls and closes dust flaps with a top tuck. This flower-petal direction needs a sequence of overlapping top panels and a final petal engagement, plus a distinct release touchpoint.

Form the offered base, load the complete contents and follow the named petal sequence. Pause before the last petal enters and inspect the top-panel/product relationship. Then open through the intended touchpoint and record which petal releases first. Ask for a located revision if the agreed route needs a different action.

Use a petal sequence and height record

The following hypothetical four-petal proposal is an original brief example. The offered design can have another panel count or arrangement.

Closure fieldIllustrative inputReview evidence
Order P1→P2→P3Named moving panels on drawing FT1Partly closed views in the offered sequence
Final petal P4Entry beneath the offered receiving overlapLast-entry detail with complete contents
Product envelopeHolder and care card in final positionsHighest projection below moving petals
Opening touchpointEdge used to begin customer releaseLoaded reopening route
Bottom B1Offered tuck or other proposed baseSupplied-state and local setup record

Handoff the actual closing route

The converter supplies the panel, overlap and base drawings. The packing owner confirms setup and closing actions with the actual contents. The buyer chooses the intended opening route or requests another sample tied to a particular petal or height question.

Use the tuck-end carton direction for a simpler end-closure comparison and the supplied-state record for preparation responsibility. product-fold-over-flap-fabric-pouch.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Fold-Over Flap Fabric Pouch Sourcing

A fold-over flap fabric pouch needs the overlap and fastening positioned around the actual primary pack. Specify the flap fold, fastener proposal and customer grip as a closure route. Review the flap fully open and closed so it clears the product during both packing and removal.

The illustration is a concept reference for a flap closure. The actual fabric, fastening and construction are confirmed by the converter.

Give the flap a defined overlap

The fabric closure catalogue lists flap, tuck and button choices, while the fabric converter leaflet identifies a square flap among fastening options. These references support the construction vocabulary. Your drawing should show the offered flap and actual fastening arrangement.

Provide the finished primary-pack height, width and thickness. Include a backing card, small jewelry box or other component that reaches the flap area. Mark the intended fold and the overlap on the closed pouch rather than specifying only an overall fabric-panel length.

Identify the proposed fastener and its anchors. State whether its location is on the outside face, beneath the flap or elsewhere on the offered construction. Include any lining or seam that contacts the contents near that point.

Review access through the moving flap

Load the actual contents with the flap fully open. Fold it through the proposed route, engage the offered fastening and inspect the complete closed shape. Reopen using the intended grip and remove the primary pack without changing its agreed orientation silently.

If the fastener requires pressure against the product, locate that action and ask for another proposal or a confirmed arrangement. If the flap springs back or obscures a grip in the observed sample, record the condition and revision. The buyer should decide the closing and access route using those specific observations.

Compare the drawstring fabric bag for channel gathering or the zippered fabric pouch for a slider/end-stop route. Keep the same product envelope in the comparison. The existing textile jewelry pouch remains the broad holder overview.

Use a flap-overlap and release table

This hypothetical jewelry primary-pack record keeps fastening as an offered field.

Closure featureExample brief inputDecision evidence
Flap F1Fold line and overlap over the complete packLoaded closed view
Fastener A1Type and anchor positions to be proposedConstruction detail and sample
Top clearanceFinished primary-pack projectionFlap travel/contact view
Lining L1Seam and lining beside the fasteningLocated contact observation
Customer gripIntended release and removal sequenceOpened loaded pouch view

Keep fastening changes attached to the drawing

The converter should return flap and fastening identities with the construction revision. The packing owner should report the actual loading and release actions. The buyer can then decide whether the overlap and access suit the primary pack, or ask for a change at a named interface.

product-foldable-lid-base-box.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Foldable Lid Base Box Sourcing

A foldable lid-and-base box uses two paperboard components that are formed separately before the lid covers the loaded base. Consider it for a small gift when a lift-off opening is wanted and the packing team can review the proposed folding work. Define both components, their supplied state and the complete product layout so the separate lid becomes part of a practical assembly plan.

Concept / inquiry direction. AI-assisted visuals explain the structure; final materials, production details and sample scope are agreed for the project.

Treat the base and lid as separate constructions

A two-piece appearance does not tell you which panels fold, lock or arrive pre-glued. Ask for the proposed base drawing and lid drawing, with the remaining local work marked on each. Identify any doubled walls, corner tabs, adhesive areas or additional parts before assigning packing responsibilities.

Measure the formed base for its usable product space, then discuss the lid overlap against the actual assembled construction. The outside dimensions of a flat blank answer a different question. Added wrapping, a holder or a card that rises above the walls can change the finished lid decision.

Decide where the formed components are stored before loading. A packing team might form both pieces in advance or assemble one complete gift at a time. Those are different workflows, with different staging questions. Record the preferred process and ask whether the supplied packing arrangement supports it.

Choose the lift-off format with its local work

Compare this direction with the rigid lid-and-base format when deciding whether local forming work belongs in the project. Both have a separate cover, but their component construction and delivery state need individual confirmation. Compare a one-piece folding carton when an attached closing flap better suits the loading process.

For an illustrative gift kit, a pouch and a care card may need a shared holder inside the base. A lid that fits an empty box may respond differently to that complete layout. Specify the removal sequence and the part the customer should grasp after the cover is lifted.

Describe the two-piece packing job

FieldRecord for review
BaseUsable formed space, wall build, locks and support for the product.
LidFormed interior, overlap depth and the intended lift-off action.
ComponentsHolder, tissue, cards and their loaded height.
AssemblyFolds, consumables, instructions and the person completing each step.
DeliveryState of both pieces, bundles and proposed carton packing.
ArtworkNamed base and lid files, print faces and finish areas.

Keep the top artwork orientation related to how the base is loaded. If a logo should face the customer at a particular opening angle, show that view in the brief. The flat and assembled scope worksheet lets the proposals identify what arrives and what remains to do.

Review one complete gift

  • Form the base and lid using the supplied instructions.
  • Inspect corners, locks, seams and the intended wall positions.
  • Load all items and extras into their proposed places.
  • Fit the lid, then lift it using the intended customer grip.
  • Remove the contents and inspect contact with the walls and holder.
  • Check artwork orientation and fold appearance on the formed pieces.

Record a base or lid correction against the appropriate drawing. If a change affects overlap or loaded height, identify the paired component that must be checked again. Approving one blank should not silently approve a different assembled pair.

Agree quantities for the complete configuration

Packrivo's order planning policy is 500 pieces per product / design. List the base, lid, holder and printed extras with their quantity and sample scope. Final materials, pricing, production conditions and delivery timing are reviewed for the agreed project.

The original foldable lid-and-base reference shows the separate folding components. Use it to understand the format, without transferring its material or commercial claims.

Home / Inserts
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Folded Box Liner Sourcing

A folded box liner is an internal component formed against the walls or selected surfaces of a box. Consider this direction when the brief needs to describe where the product or its retail pack meets the surrounding enclosure. Plan the liner's coverage, folds and loading sequence first, then decide whether a separate holder is needed to locate the contents.

Concept / inquiry direction. AI-assisted visuals explain the structure; final materials, production details and sample scope are agreed for the project.

Give the liner a defined area

Show which surfaces the proposed liner covers: side walls, a base, selected corners or another stated area. Identify the interfaces where it meets the outer box or another component. A liner may reduce the usable space, so its formed condition belongs in the interior measurement discussion.

Ask for the unfolded and formed views together. Fold tabs, seams and overlaps can change the local surface and the space available to load the product. Describe how the liner is retained, including whether the proposed construction simply rests in the enclosure or uses a specific attachment.

Mark the liner's starting orientation in the loading instructions. A rotated part can put a seam against a different product surface.

Keep the intended contact conditions visible. The product might have a sensitive finish, a projecting part or an existing retail cover. Name the surface that may touch the liner and the material information the supplier needs to address. The word “paper” does not settle contact suitability or a product-specific protection requirement.

Separate lining from locating

A paperboard holder can create cutouts or supports to position the contents. A liner introduces a different task: covering a defined area around them. An internal divider separates multiple items. Choose by the required contact and movement, and combine components only when their jobs are clear.

For an illustrative candle carton, a wall liner could be considered alongside a base support. The support determines how the vessel sits; the liner affects its relationship to the enclosure. Review their combined thickness, contact and removal rather than accepting them as two unrelated accessories.

Prepare a coverage and loading record

FieldDescribe the liner in use
Outer boxCurrent construction, usable interior and closure.
CoverageWalls or surfaces lined, open areas and the purpose of each covered area.
ConstructionMaterial proposal, folds, seams, overlaps and retention method.
ProductGeometry, finish sensitivities and named contact surfaces.
OperationsLiner assembly, product loading and customer removal sequence.
ProjectComponent quantities, destination, drawing versions and sample scope.

Keep artwork instructions tied to the surfaces that remain visible after forming. If the liner is printed, identify which folds and overlaps cover part of the graphic. A layout that looks correct while flat can present a different image inside the loaded carton.

Review the lined enclosure as one configuration

  • Form the liner and place it in the proposed outer box.
  • Inspect folds, retention and all changes to the usable interior.
  • Load the actual product and any separate supports.
  • Close the pack and inspect contact or interference with the lid.
  • Open the pack and remove the product by hand.
  • Record the contact observations and agreed next review.

If the liner shifts, bunches or prevents closure, identify the affected fold, attachment or measurement. The sample revision record keeps that issue linked to the box and liner versions. A later holder change can reopen the same contact question.

Agree component scope and quantity

Packrivo's order planning policy is 500 pieces per product / design. List the liner, enclosure and any holder separately, with their quantities and sample tasks. Final material, construction, pricing, production conditions and delivery timing are reviewed for the project.

The original box-liner structural reference distinguishes a wall-lining component from cavity-level holders. Its specifications and performance descriptions remain specific to that source.

PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Folded Tray and Sleeve Box Sourcing

A folded tray and sleeve box pairs a formed paperboard tray with an outer sliding sleeve. It can be considered for a small gift set when the reveal matters and the packing team is prepared to assemble the proposed pieces. Specify the tray folds, supplied state and loaded sliding fit together, instead of choosing a drawer-shaped image and leaving the work at the packing bench undefined.

Concept / inquiry direction. AI-assisted visuals explain the structure; final materials, production details and sample scope are agreed for the project.

Separate the two pieces and their jobs

The tray holds the contents and provides the surface from which they are removed. The sleeve surrounds that tray and establishes its opening path. Each piece has its own fold pattern, seam and artwork surfaces. Ask for the proposed construction of both, including whether the tray uses locking corners, glued parts or an additional holder.

Describe the loaded arrangement before discussing sleeve dimensions. Jewelry cards, small accessories and folded tissue can sit above the tray edge or catch at its entrance. Name the highest item and the surfaces that may touch the sleeve. The useful check is the assembled and loaded combination, rather than the tray and sleeve measured independently.

Choose how the user starts the movement: a thumb opening, a pull detail or access to an exposed tray edge. Indicate whether the tray should slide out fully. A stop, if proposed, needs its own explanation and review; it should not be inferred from a rendered picture.

Compare folded and rigid drawer construction

A rigid drawer jewelry box and a folding tray-and-sleeve direction may share an opening idea but have different component construction and preparation tasks. Compare the actual supplied state, corner formation, tray wall build and remaining local work. Those are more useful distinctions than a blanket claim that one version is cheaper or stronger.

For an illustrative gift with a necklace card and a separate pouch, the packing team must know whether the card loads before the tray is closed and whether the pouch stays below its rim. That sequence can change both the holder and the sleeve clearance. Capture the sequence while the layout is still being discussed.

State what arrives at the packing bench

Brief fieldRecord before comparing proposals
TrayFormed usable space, wall construction, corner locks and loading order.
SleeveInner opening, seam position, print faces and starting grip.
Supply stateFlat, partly formed or assembled for each component.
AssemblyWho folds, locks, glues, loads and checks the complete pack.
Additional partsHolder, card, pouch or tissue with separate quantities.
ProjectDesign quantities, destination, artwork versions and open questions.

Use the flat and assembled delivery worksheet to compare the same completed pack. Include local consumables and storage requirements in the questions. A flat drawing describes the proposed construction; it does not supply a measured assembly time or freight saving.

Check folds, loading and travel together

  • Assemble the supplied pieces using the proposed instructions.
  • Check that corners and seams reach their intended positions.
  • Load all contents, including the holder and printed extras.
  • Slide the loaded tray, checking contact at the entrance and along the travel.
  • Remove the gift by hand and inspect the fold and contact areas.
  • Record which drawing and sample versions were reviewed.

If a change is needed, identify whether it belongs to the tray, sleeve or packed contents. Widening the sleeve might alter the closed appearance; changing the tray might affect its holder. Keep those linked consequences visible before accepting the next revision.

Prepare a project-specific proposal

Packrivo's order planning policy is 500 pieces per product / design. Ask for the tray, sleeve, holder, print work and sampling to be described as separate scope items. Final material construction, pricing, production conditions and delivery timing are agreed for the reviewed configuration.

The original tray-and-sleeve structural reference shows why a folding version introduces assembly work. Its commercial terms and material specifications are not transferred to this direction.

Foldable gift boxes

Custom Folding Cartons and Gift Boxes Sourcing

Compare folding paperboard cartons and gift-box proposals by their closure, supplied state and assembly sequence.

Inquiry direction · Supplier confirmation required

Quote Details

Send the product dimensions, quantity by design and destination. Include the structure, material and artwork preferences you already know; flag open questions so supplier quotes use the same scope.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

When it may fit

It may suit a candle, small gift or retail product with a defined internal size. It does not automatically replace a separate shipper.

Details to define

  • Product dimensions, weight and orientation.
  • Inside size, closure and assembly sequence.
  • Board direction, print panels, insert/window needs.
  • Quantity, destination and sample review.

Artwork and presentation choices

Map outside, inside, tuck and glue panels on the current carton drawing. Identify the intended front face before comparing artwork in the flat and formed states.

Options to compare

  • Use expressive outside graphics, contrasting interior panels or a tactile paper look.
  • Compare a simple tuck closure with a window or insert option.
  • Separate shelf presentation from parcel protection.

Compare the closure, delivery state and finish

A folding gift-box brief needs separate decisions about the structure, the work left after delivery and the decorated surfaces. Keep those decisions on the same drawing and complete contents list.

DecisionIdentify in the proposalReview on the candidate
Tuck-end closureLoading end, customer opening, tuck direction and depth, receiving feature and intended reopening.Close and reopen the formed carton with the complete product, insert and card present.
Flat or formed deliverySupplied parts, prepared joints, remaining folds or fasteners, assembly location and responsible operator.Follow the supplied setup sequence before loading; retain unresolved steps rather than silently fixing them.
Decorative finishArtwork revision, named panel, proposed process, finish boundary and physical appearance reference.Compare the finish on the formed box, including folds, edges, glue areas and closure contact points.

For a tuck-end proposal, compare same-side end flaps with opposing tuck directions. Keep the printed front fixed while identifying the loading and customer-opening ends.

A collapsible magnetic gift box is a separate construction to compare, not another name for every folding carton. Ask for its own folded and formed views. A decorative finish likewise does not establish the underlying fold pattern.

Supplier confirmation needed

Confirm dieline, board specification, closure, folds, glue zones and finished size with the supplier. Sample review is needed for the assembled form.

Project details to agree

Final materials, construction, price, sample scope and delivery timing are confirmed for the agreed project with the relevant supplier.

When to discuss this direction

For a printed carton brief where the buyer can define the folded shape, loading direction and closure. The concept does not prove a suitable board grade or load capacity; heavier or fragile products need a specific protection review.

Quote inputs to prepare

  • Actual product size, weight, loading direction and required internal space.
  • Carton panel dimensions, closure style and delivery flat or assembled.
  • Board and printing preferences, artwork and any insert requirement.
  • Quantity, SKU variants, destination and assembly responsibility.

What to approve on a sample

  • Fold lines, tabs and closure fit on a physical sample.
  • Product loading/removal and space for the agreed contents.
  • Artwork alignment across folds and the approved color reference.
  • Assembly steps, packed carton count and agreed protection checks.

Move this packaging project forward

Packrivo helps turn this direction into a clear brief, coordinate supplier questions, compare responses and review sample evidence against your product.

Use the folded-box specification checklist to prepare the relevant details.

Plan the quotation and sample scope

Request the box or pouch, insert where needed, decoration, sampling, packing and delivery as separate cost items. Confirm the quoted specification, quantity, currency, trade terms and validity before comparing offers. MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design.

Agree what a structural sample will check and which printed or finished sample is needed before production approval. Record the specification and sample version so a later change does not silently replace an earlier approval.

Keep market references separate from supplier confirmation and a project quotation. Use the quotation comparison checklist and sample approval checklist before approving the next step.

Frequently asked questions

What comes before artwork?

Structure and finished dimensions come first. Request the supplier dieline, then map artwork to the approved panels.

Is the shown structure confirmed?

No. This is a visual inquiry concept. Structure, materials, sample, commercial terms and market suitability need project-specific confirmation.

Custom Folding Gift Box Sourcing

MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design. Plan the quantity for each design in your brief.

Choose a folding gift box from its formed size, opening and assembly steps, then confirm the actual state in which it will be delivered.

Concept direction · Feasibility unverified

Your starting brief

Send the gift contents, their packed dimensions and weight, the preferred opening, and who will assemble the box. Say whether an insert, tissue or a card will be inside; the outside appearance alone does not define a fold pattern.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

Define the gift set and assembly point

  • Measure the complete gift arrangement rather than the largest product alone; include wrap, tissue and cards.
  • State the usable interior, closure preference and the order in which contents will be loaded.
  • Identify who forms the box, installs the insert and completes the final pack at the delivery destination.

Compare the proposed folding structures

A folding carton and a collapsible gift-box structure can have different assembly sequences. Ask for the proposed drawing and a demonstration of the delivered and formed states. Keep a lid-and-base direction as an alternative when the buyer prefers separate components; compare the packing steps before choosing.

If your starting point is a reference image, use the image-to-brief workflow to separate the desired appearance from the fold pattern and other details the supplier still needs to propose.

Check the box in both delivered and formed states

  • Form the supplied candidate using the proposed assembly sequence and note any steps that need clarification.
  • Load the complete gift set, close the box and review how it opens again; keep the selected insert and card with the sample.
  • Compare the demonstrated delivery state with the written scope. Record who supplies any fastening parts and who completes assembly.

MOQ and project scope

MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design. State the quantity for each design, not just the combined order total. Packrivo helps organize the brief and supplier questions. The relevant supplier confirms the proposed materials, construction, price, sample scope and delivery timing for the agreed configuration.

Include your destination and any open inputs. If a detail is not yet known, name who will provide it before the next review.

Before you send a brief

Can I use my own branding?

Include your desired logo placement, print surfaces and colors. Final artwork must use the approved supplier dieline and pass proof review.

Can you make exactly what the picture shows?

The picture is an AI-assisted concept, not a production promise. Structure, materials, tolerances and finishing need supplier review and a physical sample.

What happens after an inquiry?

A person reviews the brief and missing details. Supplier checks and sample or quotation discussions follow only after the next steps are agreed.

Distinguish a visual style from a confirmed collapsible structure before discussing freight.

Custom Four-Corner Display Tray Sourcing

Plan a four corner display tray around the units that customers will remove, then review its front opening with a full and reduced display. Confirm the prepared corner construction and supplied state. The tray's outside shape doesn't show whether the first or last unit can be gripped cleanly.

This direction focuses on a prepared tray and the customer-facing cutout. The unit arrangement, restocking method and front-wall profile should be decided together. Retail fit and distribution protection are separate questions.

Confirm the corners before drawing the display front

PakFactory's four corner display reference describes a collapsible display with four pre-glued corners. Use that detail as a structural reference, then request the actual corner and front-cutout drawing for your project.

Show the tray before and after setup. Identify the four prepared corners and ask how the front profile is formed. A drawing should make clear which sections stay attached, fold or are removed.

Within the foldable packaging family, this configuration answers a display task. If customers receive the whole box, review that complete-pack action separately from a tray that stays on the counter.

Arrange the sale-ready units

Provide unit dimensions with any outer card, lid or wrap attached. Show the intended row count and facing direction on a top view. Include any divider or backing piece so the layout describes the actual display contents.

For a hypothetical counter display of jewelry-card packs, the first row may sit behind a low front wall. Ask a reviewer to pick a unit from that row without lifting the tray. Repeat the action after the first row is gone and only the back row remains.

Restocking deserves its own action. State whether staff refill from above, replace the whole tray or move stock forwards. A low front cutout that works for removal may still leave a different question about arranging the remaining units.

Record access as the display empties

Use identical unit orientation in each state. The record is an observation tool rather than a sales prediction.

Display stateUnit to removeObservation to capture
FullFront corner and front centerFinger route above or around front wall
ReducedRemaining rear rowReach and neighbouring unit movement
Last unitFinal intended positionVisibility and grip without tipping tray
RefillReplacement unitsEntry route and final facing position

Photograph the starting state before each removal. If a unit falls or moves, record which action caused it. Don't hide that movement by rearranging the tray before taking the evidence photo.

Sample the cutout with the formed corners

Confirm whether the tray arrives flat with corners prepared and who forms it. Load the sample only after all corners are in the intended position. A wall that is still partly collapsed can change the front profile during the trial.

Review the proposed material, board caliper and unit load as a configuration. If the front wall, divider or unit size changes, repeat the depletion record. Avoid assigning a capacity from the structure name or borrowing a supplier's promotional strength statement.

Check that artwork remains visible at the chosen front height. The customer grip has priority over fitting a large printed message into a panel that needs cutting away.

When a proposed cutout has a curved or stepped front profile, mark the unit positions beside its high and low sections. Review grip at both locations. A center opening photo can miss a corner unit behind a taller section. Keep that extra position in the depletion record if it belongs to the intended retail arrangement.

Bring the display states to the brief

Send your unit envelope, row layout, front-cutout sketch, refill method, quantity and destination through Get a Quote. The minimum is 500 pieces per design. The structure, components, sample scope, price and timing are confirmed for the specific project.

PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Four-Corner Pre-Glued Carton Sourcing

Review a four corner pre glued carton by confirming its prepared base joints and attached lid on the actual drawing. Form the empty structure before loading, then check the lid with all contents in place. The delivered state and forming sequence belong in the enquiry alongside the finished dimensions.

This direction focuses on a collapsible base with a hinged lid and four prepared corners. It should be compared through setup and closure actions. The number of corners doesn't establish a performance ranking.

Identify prepared corners and the lid fold

The four corner box reference describes a collapsible hinged-lid structure with four pre-glued corners. Request the supplier's proposal to identify those joints and the lid's actual edge details.

Keep the base joints separate from the lid hinge on the drawing. Mark the position the base should reach after forming. Ask whether any lid-side detail requires a manual tuck or other action beyond lifting the base walls.

A six corner pre glued carton adds another prepared-corner configuration to compare. Make that comparison with supplied and formed views, not an assumption that one style is automatically stronger.

Form the empty base before checking the product

Start with the sample in the agreed delivered state. Follow the proposed forming instruction and photograph each base corner afterwards. Note any corner that remains partly folded or needs a separate movement.

For a hypothetical small gift set, form the tray first, then place a card holder and accessory inside. This sequence helps show whether the holder interferes with a corner or whether the corner itself was incomplete before loading.

Raise and lower the attached lid while the base remains empty. Then repeat with the complete contents. Record the difference if the lid changes position when a product, tissue fold or card is added.

Keep a base-and-lid comparison record

Use one sample revision for all rows. Include photographs from the supplied and final loaded states.

PartEmpty-state checkLoaded-state check
Four base jointsEach reaches its intended formed positionHolder or product leaves that position unchanged
Lid hingeMovement and resting positionClearance above the complete contents
Lid edgesProposed closing actionContact with walls, card or wrap
Customer accessStarting grip locationProduct removal after lid opens

If a lid edge catches, name the contacting part and the stage. A request to add depth may solve a product-height issue but won't necessarily resolve a base corner formed incorrectly.

Agree the material and packing handoff

State the board grade, caliper, print surfaces and prepared joints proposed for the final sample. If those details remain open, leave them as explicit questions. A material substituted for an early mock-up should be named in its record.

The delivery-state guide helps define who forms the carton and adds the contents. Keep separate components visible in that scope rather than treating the folded box as a complete gift set.

Review corner formation, closure and removal as observations. Agree any weight, handling or distribution requirement separately; a clean lid fit doesn't demonstrate protection. Final outside dimensions should be checked in the loaded closed state if that is the specified reference condition.

Keep lid-edge formation in the setup instruction if the supplier proposal includes it. The phrase 'four prepared corners' should not conceal a separate lid action. A reviewer should be able to identify the finished base and the ready-to-close lid as two checkpoints, even when both belong to the same continuous blank.

Submit the joint and lid record

Send the marked drawing, supplied-state request, complete contents, quantity and destination through Get a Quote. The minimum is 500 pieces per design. Construction, sample work and commercial terms need project confirmation.
