Mailer boxes

Custom Mailer Box Sourcing

Describe the complete packed product before comparing a mailer structure, its weight, delivery state and printed surfaces. A front-tuck corrugated box is one option to review.

Inquiry direction · Supplier confirmation required

Quote Details

Send the product dimensions, quantity by design and destination. Include the structure, material and artwork preferences you already know; flag open questions so supplier quotes use the same scope.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

When it may fit

It may suit ecommerce parcels, subscriptions or gift sets when a corrugated box format is preferred. It is not proof of transit performance by itself.

Details to define

  • Product bundle dimensions, weight and order variants.
  • Inside size, tuck closure and insert/void-fill need.
  • Corrugated specification for supplier review, print panels and pack sequence.
  • Quantity, destination and sample requirements.

Artwork and presentation choices

Decide which artwork the buyer sees before opening and which appears inside the mailer. Mark folds and sealing areas on the same drawing used for the loaded-pack review.

Options to compare

  • Try a bold exterior pattern, high-contrast band or full-color interior print.
  • Keep graphic elements clear of folds and adhesive areas.
  • Separate doorstep presentation from shipping test requirements.

Compare weight, delivery and printing against one packed system

The front-tuck corrugated mailer shown on this page is one structural direction. A request for a lighter box, flat delivery or printed surfaces still needs an identified closure and complete contents; those attributes do not define a new structure by themselves.

Option to compareKeep in the same briefQuestion to resolve
Lower proposed box weightComplete product and retail pack, accessories, wrap or insert, loaded dimensions, destination and handling route.What construction and sample review support this proposal for the same contents? Lower box weight alone does not establish protection.
Flat deliveryDelivered parts and outline, formed interior, closure, insert installation and any fastening components.Who forms the box, fits the insert, loads it and closes it, and what instructions arrive with the parts?
Printed mailerCurrent drawing and artwork, inside and outside panels, opening orientation and the physical color reference.Which print areas cross folds, meet seals or sit beneath a shipping label, and what remains visible after packing?

Request each offered closure by name and drawing. Do not label an alternative front-tuck merely because it shares the same weight or printed appearance. Keep the mailer and fitted insert together in the loaded review, while retaining any distribution-performance evaluation as its own scope.

Compare flat and assembled offers against the same finished arrangement, with remaining local work identified. Review printed panels on the formed candidate rather than treating a flat screen preview as physical color or finished-pack evidence.

Supplier confirmation needed

Confirm structure, material, closure, assembled dimensions and sample with a supplier. Any transit or stacking claim needs an agreed test and evidence.

Project details to agree

Final materials, construction, price, sample scope and delivery timing are confirmed for the agreed project with the relevant supplier.

When to discuss this direction

For a corrugated mailer brief with a front-tuck opening. Board, fit, packed weight and the shipping route must be reviewed together; the rendered box does not establish a tested transit result.

Quote inputs to prepare

  • Product dimensions, packed weight and any inner protection.
  • Finished internal dimensions, board preference and closure details.
  • Printed surfaces, artwork and any labels or handling requirements.
  • Quantity, variant split, destination and delivery flat or assembled.

What to approve on a sample

  • Assembly, front-tuck closure and repeated opening.
  • Product restraint and clearance in the complete packed configuration.
  • Print alignment and finished dimensions on the approved sample.
  • Protection checks matched to the product and proposed shipping route.

Move this packaging project forward

Packrivo helps turn this direction into a clear brief, coordinate supplier questions, compare responses and review sample evidence against your product.

Use the mailer protection review guide to prepare the relevant details.

Plan the quotation and sample scope

Request the box or pouch, insert where needed, decoration, sampling, packing and delivery as separate cost items. Confirm the quoted specification, quantity, currency, trade terms and validity before comparing offers. MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design.

Agree what a structural sample will check and which printed or finished sample is needed before production approval. Record the specification and sample version so a later change does not silently replace an earlier approval.

Keep market references separate from supplier confirmation and a project quotation. Use the quotation comparison checklist and sample approval checklist before approving the next step.

Frequently asked questions

Can a mailer box also be a presentation box?

A box may serve both roles, but the presentation and delivery requirements should be reviewed separately for the complete configuration.

Is the material or use claim confirmed?

No. This is an inquiry candidate. Exact composition, market suitability, supplier feasibility, project price and timing and performance need evidence.

PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Full-Flap Auto-Bottom Carton Sourcing

A full-flap auto-bottom carton needs two base records: how the prepared bottom forms, and where the coverage flap sits beneath the product. Identify the flap on the offered drawing, then review its overlap and contact with the complete contents. This gives the supplier a specific base question instead of a request for a generally heavier box.

This concept direction requires supplier confirmation of the offered base drawing and material proposal; the illustration explains the coverage interface.

Locate the coverage flap inside the formed carton

The full-flap auto-bottom reference names this construction. Esko also illustrates full-flap auto-bottom carton configurations in its ArtiosCAD style catalogue. Use those references to identify the idea, then obtain the actual blank offered for your gift. The position and shape of its coverage flap must be visible on that drawing.

Ask for an inside base view and an underside view. Mark the coverage flap, its fold, the underlying prepared joints and any exposed overlap. Those views answer different questions: the underside explains erection, while the inside shows what the loaded product touches.

Measure the product footprint in its finished primary packaging. Include a projecting candle-jar rim, a jewelry backing card or any separate accessory. State which object sits directly on the base and which object is carried by an insert. That contact map helps avoid approving a neat empty carton that behaves differently after loading.

Separate erection from product contact

Compare the auto-bottom carton when the main concern is the prepared base opening into position. The full-flap configuration adds a coverage and overlap decision. It deserves its own page only when the offered drawing and actual product contact make that additional decision meaningful.

Start the sample review with the carton empty. Form it using the supplied instructions, photograph the interior flap position, then load the complete set in the intended order. Record whether a flap edge catches the contents, whether a corner rests on an overlap and whether an insert changes the contact location. Leave any load or distribution evaluation as a separately agreed task.

Use a coverage and contact record

The following entries are a hypothetical candle-gift planning example. Replace them with the proposed drawing and observations; they are not completed sample results.

Base interfaceExample brief entryEvidence to request
Coverage flap B1Show B1 beneath the jar and identify its foldOffered blank plus inside base view
Prepared joint J1Identify factory preparation separately from B1Underside view and supplied state
Jar footprintFinished jar is the direct contact itemProduct dimensions and contact map
Accessory insertCard holder sits beside the jarLoaded interior photograph
Overlap questionKeep any catching edge open for reviewNamed observation and proposed revision

Give the next question to the right owner

The converter should supply the flap and joint drawing. Your packing owner should confirm the erection and loading order, including whether the carton arrives prepared or needs an additional action. The buyer then decides which observed contacts need a revision or a further sample. A single closed-carton photograph cannot replace these three records.

Use the folding carton direction to compare the broader box choice, and the flat and assembled delivery method to record preparation responsibility.

Send the offered base view, product footprint, insert arrangement and open overlap question through Get a Quote. Packrivo’s minimum is 500 pieces per design. Structure, material, sample scope and commercial terms are confirmed for the project after those inputs are clear.

product-full-overlap-seal-end-carton.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Full-Overlap Seal End Carton Sourcing

Specify a full overlap seal end carton by its end-flap coverage and the operation used to seal those flaps. Name who loads the carton, who seals each end and what equipment they use. Confirm the process before approving a structure that depends on a separate sealing step.

This direction is distinct from a carton that closes by tucking a flap into the body. Its brief needs both geometry and production handoff. An assembled concept can hide the operation that your packing bench would have to complete.

Show coverage at each end

The full overlap seal end reference describes fuller end flaps and warns that large-volume assembly requires glue equipment. Use those statements to ask process questions, not to assume a particular supplier machine or your own production capability.

Request an end view showing the flap order and coverage. Label the intended sealing areas separately from printed artwork. The proposal should explain which surfaces meet and which flap closes last.

Compare the existing tuck-end carton direction if a reopenable end action is central to the product. Here, review the sealed-end opening route explicitly rather than calling it the same closure.

Assign the sealing work before asking for samples

State whether the supplier seals one end before delivery or both ends after packing the product. If your team performs the final seal, describe the equipment and method available at the actual packing location. Mark unknown equipment as an open question.

A hypothetical accessory bundle might be inserted through one open end after the other has been prepared. The operator then closes the remaining flaps and completes the agreed seal. Identify the adhesive system, equipment and responsible packing operation in the supplier proposal before adopting that sequence.

Ask how the sample should represent the proposed sealing method. A manually assembled appearance sample and a process-representative sample answer different questions. Record the purpose of each if both are proposed.

Use a coverage and responsibility record

Attach the end views and process description to the same drawing revision. Fill each responsibility with an actual role, not an assumed factory step.

StageGeometry required in the proposalResponsible operation
First endFlap order and coverageWho prepares and seals it
LoadingOpen-end envelope and product orientationWho inserts the complete contents
Second endLast flap and sealing surfacesMethod, equipment and operator
Customer openingIntended access routeInstruction and acceptable opened condition

The record makes a missing process visible before price comparison. A quotation for empty flat cartons can't be treated as a quotation for packed, sealed units.

Inspect the loaded seam and opening

Confirm the supplied state, material and caliper. View the end seam after the proposed operation with complete contents present. Photograph any flap lift, uneven placement or visible contact with the product.

Open the sample using the intended customer route. Record where opening begins and how the product is removed. If the pack is intended for a single opening, say so in the brief; if reuse is desired, ask whether another closure direction is more appropriate.

These observations don't demonstrate seal integrity, tamper evidence or transit protection. Any such requirement needs a defined evaluation and responsible evidence. Keep vendor promotional protection language out of the approval record.

Record the quantity being discussed for the sealing operation as well as the carton design quantity. A small appearance sample may be assembled under different conditions from a production run. Ask the supplier to state which conditions its sample represents, then keep that explanation with the seam photographs before using them as an approval reference.

Send the end process with the product

product-full-overlap-slotted-outer-carto.post_content:
Home / Mailer Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Full-Overlap Slotted Outer Carton Sourcing

Specify a full overlap slotted outer carton with a closed-end drawing that shows the outer flaps overlapping. Define the flap order and sealing method for both top and bottom. Confirm actual overlap on the proposal instead of assuming the format name fixes the coverage or the finished pack's performance.

This direction concerns flap geometry in a corrugated outer pack. Keep the complete contents and handling route in the brief. The extra layers at an end do not by themselves verify performance for your product.

Read the actual coverage drawing

Packaging Corporation of America's basic box styles reference describes long flaps that largely overlap in a full overlap slotted container. Its catalogue dimensions and performance statements are not universal specifications for your carton.

Request top and bottom views with the outer-flap closing order marked. Show which flap finishes outside and where the sealing surface lies. Request the overlap dimensions on both the inside and outside views of the proposed carton.

Compare a snap bottom slotted outer carton when manual interlocking base setup is an option. Here, focus on overlap coverage and the associated sealing operation, not a strength comparison based on names.

Match the seal to the packing operation

State who forms the bottom, loads the contents and seals the top. Describe the available sealing method and equipment. If these are unknown, leave them as open process questions before comparing proposals.

A hypothetical outer carton of gift sets might be filled at a small packing bench. Staff need an instruction that shows the bottom flap order before loading and the top order afterwards. Reversing the outer-flap order can also change the visible seam and label placement.

Provide the full packed weight and arrangement, including any dividers or void fill. Keep shipping labels and other printed information outside the unresolved sealing area until the operation is agreed.

Use a top-and-bottom map

Record the actual proposal revision. A photograph of one closed end should not be treated as evidence for the other.

LocationCoverage inputSealing operation and responsible party
Bottom inner flapsFinal folded positionsOrder before outer flaps
Bottom outer flapsOverlap shown on end viewFinal outside flap and seal path
Top outer flapsOverlap with full contents loadedClosing order and sealing method
Receiving openingSeam and tool-access area if relevantOpening route clear of products

The record gives a reviewer somewhere to put an observation such as 'top overlap changed after loading'. That is more useful than asking for a stronger version without identifying the changed geometry.

Review supplied state and complete-pack evidence

Confirm the delivered form and side-seam preparation. Include the proposed corrugated construction and dimension reference condition. Inspect both ends after the loaded sample is closed using the agreed method.

Open the carton along the intended receiving route and check the contents before rearranging them. If a cutting tool is part of the operation, its safe route needs a responsible instruction suited to the actual pack.

Use the outer packaging collection for broader format options. Request a separate evaluation proposal for the intended distribution conditions. The overlap map is a configuration review, not proof of cushioning, stacking strength or transit protection.

If the carton carries an outside orientation instruction, review it against the actual final flap and seam position. A packing team may turn the carton during bottom formation and leave it in another orientation for loading. The end map should restore the intended top, front and receiving route before labels or artwork are treated as fixed.

Send both ends with the brief

product-gable-top-carry-carton.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Gable Top Carry Carton Sourcing

A gable-top carton forms a raised top with a carrying feature above the main box body. Consider this direction for a gift that will be handed over and carried, when the proposed handle, top closure and base can be reviewed with the full contents. Describe the carry action alongside the product layout so the handle becomes a defined part of the structure.

Concept / inquiry direction. AI-assisted visuals explain the structure; final materials, production details and sample scope are agreed for the project.

Follow the structure through the top

The raised top changes the carton silhouette and the space available for loading and closing. Ask which panels create the handle, how those panels join and which tabs or folds hold the top in position. A drawing should show the opening before loading and the closed carrying state.

Keep the usable product cavity separate from the raised top. A vessel or accessory should be described in the position it occupies inside the main body, including its holder and any card. Then identify whether a projecting part comes near the sloping top panels or the handle attachment.

Describe the person’s carrying action. The opening needs to suit the intended grip, while the assembled package has to be assessed for its actual weight and handling conditions. Ask the responsible supplier to propose the construction and relevant review. Avoid selecting a material or accepting a carrying claim from the handle’s appearance alone.

Compare carrying and presentation tasks

A standard folding carton can place the emphasis on loading and end closure. A gable format brings the carry feature into the carton itself. A separate gift bag and tissue set creates a different component list and handoff sequence. Compare the complete job rather than treating the bag or handle as interchangeable decoration.

For an illustrative candle gift, the jar, insert and information card need to be inside the layout used for review. The top panels might need space to fold around that arrangement. The carry action also depends on the base and the insert, so the handle review should refer to the same complete configuration.

Prepare the carry and loading brief

Brief fieldSpecify or identify as open
Product layoutComplete contents, weight, display orientation and projecting parts.
BodyUsable interior, loading opening, base and holder arrangement.
Raised topPanel construction, closing sequence and space above the product.
Carry featureGrip opening, attachment, intended handling and review requirement.
PresentationPrint orientation on the body and top, including folded areas.
ScopeQuantity by design, supplied state, assembly responsibility and destination.

The measurement method worksheet helps separate the body cavity, overall height and grip opening. Name their locations so a quote or sample drawing does not silently substitute one measurement for another.

Review the complete carry sequence

  • Form the base and top using the proposed instructions.
  • Load the product, holder and printed extras in the intended order.
  • Close the top and inspect tabs, folds and any attachment points.
  • Review the agreed carry action with the actual loaded configuration.
  • Open the package and remove the product using the intended route.
  • Inspect the handle, base and contact areas after that review.

Record an issue at its location: a top panel catching a card, an uncomfortable grip or a tab that does not reach its intended position. A change to the handle can affect the top artwork and the supplied flat layout, so keep the structural and print versions paired.

Agree the project conditions

Packrivo's order planning policy is 500 pieces per product / design. Separate the carton, holder and additional components in the proposal. Final construction, material, pricing, production conditions and delivery timing are agreed against the reviewed brief.

The original gable-box structural reference provides a named example of the raised-top format. A project-specific carrying review is still needed for the proposed contents and construction.

Home / Mailer Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Gift Hang Tag Sourcing

Specify a gift hang tag with a marked attachment hole, a separate cord or fastener record and copy placed for the assembled view. Review how it hangs during packing and how the customer removes it. A tag artwork file alone doesn't define the connection or which face remains readable.

This concept needs confirmation of tag material, hole and attachment supply. Keep the joining component identified rather than assuming it is included with the printed card.

Draw the hole and attachment separately

The paper tag reference describes a die-cut attachment hole. Ask for its position and outline on the proposed tag drawing. Identify the cord, loop, tie or other fastener as a separate component with its own supply scope.

Show where the attachment goes on the product or gift pack. Mark sensitive or finished surfaces as questions for review if they meet the connection. The tag should not be treated as the same component as an unattached information card.

Locate copy in the assembled view

Provide the actual required wording and artwork owner. Show the tag's front, back and packed orientation. If the tag turns while attached, decide which information must remain available without assuming a fixed face.

For a hypothetical gift box, a tag could hang from a ribbon outside the lid. Review the face shown before opening and the route for removing the tag. The attachment knot or loop may cover a different area from the hole itself.

Use the artwork handoff method to keep hole placement and copy tied to the current drawing. A changed hole or tag shape can reopen artwork without changing the words.

Use a tag connection record

Keep tag, attachment and gift-pack identities together. The table records the visible relationship at each stage.

Connection fieldInputReview evidence
HoleOutline and drawing positionCurrent tag dieline
AttachmentSeparate component and joining methodAssembled front/back view
Pack locationGift part or ribbon connectionPacked tag position
CopySupplied wording and reading faceVisibility at intended stage
RemovalCustomer actionDetached tag and pack afterwards

A supplier reply confirming the tag stock doesn't close the cord or fastener field. Keep component counts and matching design grouping visible in the quotation scope.

Check a specific hidden-copy question

In the hypothetical map, call the hole H1, loop L1 and care message C1. If L1 covers C1 while the tag hangs, record that assembled view before moving the copy. Ask whether the attachment route or artwork should change.

Review the proposed material sample with the actual hole and connection. If the tag shape changes, inspect the attachment and removal again. Avoid presenting a clean concept hole as evidence of a finished production edge.

Any retention, compatibility or handling requirement needs a separate agreed method. This record covers the connection and information view without claiming tamper evidence or a rated attachment.

Send the tag and joining component

product-gusset-folder-carton.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Gusset Folder Carton Sourcing

Plan a gusset folder around the actual thickness of its complete contents. Review the side folds and lock with both the thinnest and thickest intended pack configurations. A folder that closes empty doesn't show whether a thicker bundle leaves the gussets or opening route in the right position.

Use this direction for a flat product or document-style bundle whose thickness is part of the purchase brief. Confirm the actual folder construction, lock and delivered form on the supplier proposal. It isn't a general claim that one size will fit every bundle.

Describe the contents as a stack

PakFactory's gusset folder reference identifies expanding sides for flat contents. Use that relationship to describe the side-fold job. The expansion you can accept for your own pack requires a drawing and loaded sample.

Measure the entire stack in its packed condition, including backing board, wrap and any raised component. Record the stack's largest thickness and where that point occurs. A folded booklet and a flat card with a small attached item don't create the same envelope.

For a hypothetical gift stationery set, the basic bundle might contain a few cards, while the larger bundle adds envelopes and a care sheet. Those are two named configurations, not two estimates of the same product.

Review the side folds at each thickness

Load the thinner bundle first and place the folder in the intended closed orientation. Observe the gussets from the side. Note loose areas, panel bowing or contents that sit at a different depth than the drawing suggests.

Use a fresh comparison sample for the thicker bundle if repeated folding has changed the first. Inspect the same locations, then open the lock and remove the contents. Include the customer's likely grip rather than lifting the stack out through an unplanned gap.

Compare other folding formats if the product needs a fixed-depth cavity instead. This direction's core decision is how a defined thickness range meets side-fold geometry and the lock.

Keep a two-configuration comparison

Write actual measurements in the blank parts of your own record. The table identifies the fields; it doesn't provide universal allowances.

RecordThinner bundleThicker bundle
ContentsList each included pieceList additions and changed parts
ThicknessMeasure packed high pointMeasure packed high point
Gusset positionPhotograph both side foldsRepeat the same views
Lock and accessRecord closure and removal actionRecord contact or obstruction

A thicker pack may need a different structure rather than more force at the lock. Send the observation to the supplier with the drawing revision and ask which part needs changing.

Confirm preparation and material together

Ask how the folder arrives and whether the side folds or joining areas are already prepared. State who forms it, inserts the stack and closes the lock. A packing instruction should show the side folds before the cover is pushed down.

Review the proposed board and caliper against the actual fold pattern. If artwork spans a gusset, view it loaded at both thicknesses before confirming its position. A flat print proof alone can't show which part of that artwork becomes hidden in a fold.

Keep the sample checks on fit, formation, opening and presentation. Don't treat them as measured protection or durability. Any handling evaluation should name the conditions, contents and agreed acceptance rule separately.

A bundle with one local raised part needs a side sketch as well as its maximum thickness. Show whether that part sits beside a gusset or under the cover. Two stacks with the same maximum thickness can place their high points differently. Keep that position fixed in the thin-and-thick comparison instead of treating one number as the complete contents description.

Send the thickness range, not a vague size

product-hanging-tab-retail-carton.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Hanging Tab Retail Carton Sourcing

A hanging-tab carton adds a display panel or attachment above or beside a folding box so the pack can be presented on a retail fixture. Consider this direction when the product should remain inside a carton while the retailer hangs the pack. Brief the fixture interface, assembled weight and product position together, then review the complete package in the intended display arrangement.

Compare an integral five-panel hanger with an attached hanging feature

In a five-panel hanger proposal, identify the projecting hanger panel separately from the carton body and its end closures. Show its fold, hole and printed face on the actual drawing. A projecting hanger should not be mistaken for the flap used to load or close the box.

Hanging featureConstruction to identifyAssembly question
Integral projecting panelPanel outline, fold, hang opening and relationship to the carton closure.Does the panel remain raised or fold at another stage, and which end receives the product?
Separately attached featureAdditional part, attachment position, joining proposal and receiving carton surface.What arrives attached, what remains to join and who performs that work?

Provide the real hook or fixture, surrounding display space and complete packed weight. Review three actions with the same loaded sample: resting on the fixture, lifting the pack off it and opening the contents. Record a problem against the action and interface where it occurs.

Keep a fixture observation tied to its sample and load. Neither the structure name nor a catalogue picture establishes a hanging capacity for a different product or material.

Concept / inquiry direction. AI-assisted visuals explain the structure; final materials, production details and sample scope are agreed for the project.

Describe the fixture before the tab

Record the retailer's hook or fixture details and the space around the display. A generic hanging hole does not define its shape, position or clearance. Show where the loaded carton should sit, which face the customer sees and how the carton is taken off the fixture.

Ask whether the proposed hanging feature is part of the paperboard blank or a separately attached component. That changes the material list, assembly work and review of the attachment. Identify any fold between the display panel and the box body so the intended hanging position is clear in the drawing.

Keep the hanging location related to the complete product layout. Jewelry cards, pouches or other holders may put the contents to one side. Record the loaded weight and orientation rather than assuming the front artwork and the actual displayed position will align.

Keep retail access separate from loading

The box still needs a defined loading and opening route. An operator may load through one end while a customer opens another. A hanging panel near that opening could affect either action. Show the top or end closure and the tab on the same proposed construction.

Compare a tuck-end carton when a shelf position is sufficient. The hanging direction adds a fixture and display review to that task. For an accessory displayed openly on a card, a different mounting arrangement may be useful; a carton is a separate choice about enclosure and information space.

Prepare the display specification

InputWhat the supplier needs
FixtureHook or fixture geometry, available space and removal movement.
Hanging featureIntegral or attached, position, hole shape and proposed construction.
Packed contentsWeight, layout, holder, projections and orientation.
Carton accessLoading end, retail opening, closure and remaining assembly.
ArtworkVisible faces, fold zones, required copy and barcode position.
ProjectDesign quantities, destination, display conditions and sample scope.

Use a simple layout drawing to connect the hole, box and product. If the retailer provides a fixture specification, keep its name or revision with the packaging files. The artwork handoff checklist helps retain that relationship as the panels and print files are prepared.

Review the loaded display and customer action

  • Assemble and load the proposed carton with every included component.
  • Place it on the intended fixture and inspect its resting position.
  • Check hole access, tab folds and any attachment interface.
  • Read the visible information from the expected customer view.
  • Remove the pack, open it and take out the product.
  • Record the agreed display review and any change required.

For an illustrative earrings-and-pouch pack, the hanger position and the card layout could both affect how it rests. If the pack tilts, the next discussion should identify the layout or hanging interface to review. Increasing a hole or changing the tab alone might not address the complete arrangement.

Plan one reviewable retail pack

Packrivo's order planning policy is 500 pieces per product / design. Identify the carton, hanging component if separate, holder and sampling work in the proposal. Material, production conditions, pricing and delivery timing are confirmed for the project.

product-header-card-bag-topper.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Header Card Bag Topper Sourcing

Specify a header card bag topper as a connection between a folded card and the actual bag mouth. Show the attachment method, fold position and display fixture together. Review customer removal separately from how the assembled pack hangs or stands, because the card alone doesn't define either action.

This direction is for a product presented in a bag with a separate top card. The proposal must define the bag, card and joining work. A card catalogue entry doesn't confirm a complete bag pack or any hygiene, barrier or tamper-evidence function.

Give the card and bag separate identities

The header card catalogue reference establishes the named component. Use your own drawing to show how it joins your bag. Keep the bag mouth, card fold and attachment points on separate labeled layers.

Measure the filled bag at the point where the card will be fitted. Record any folded bag edge, seam or product bulge near the connection. A flat bag width is insufficient if the mouth changes shape when filled.

Compare this component with folding box directions when the product needs a cavity instead of a bag presentation. The header-card job is to define the card-to-bag connection and visible information area.

Choose how the pack will be presented

State whether the pack hangs from a peg, stands in a tray or lies on a shelf. If it hangs, provide the actual fixture geometry or a usable reference. The hole's position and shape should come from that fixture and the assembled pack, not from a generic artwork template.

A hypothetical bag of decorative gift tags might hang from a store peg. Its header has a front face, rear face and fold at the top. Review the complete pack on the proposed fixture, then lift it off using the action expected from a customer.

Ask who applies the connection and with what method. If staples, adhesive or another joining detail is proposed, confirm its exact location and responsibility. Don't describe the connection as sealing the bag unless a separate, verified bag closure has been specified.

Check all three interfaces

Fill the matrix with the proposed component revisions. It keeps a card-only artwork approval from closing questions about the bag or fixture.

InterfaceBrief inputSample action
Card fold to bag mouthFilled mouth outline and fold positionFold around the actual filled bag
Attachment to both layersJoining method and locationInspect front, rear and bag interior as relevant
Hole to fixtureFixture shape and pack orientationPlace and remove the complete pack
Customer to contentsIntended opening instructionRemove card and access product as proposed

Record which information is hidden at the fold or attachment. Keep necessary instructions in the visible area rather than expecting the customer to unfold the card while it remains attached.

Agree delivery and assembly responsibilities

State whether cards arrive flat or folded and whether bags are separate. Request a sample of the assembled connection if that work belongs to the proposed supply scope. Keep the product count and orientation fixed during comparison.

Inspect the card after fitting and after customer removal. Note torn edges, misalignment and any attachment that interferes with the bag opening. These are observation fields for a sample review; they do not establish hanging capacity or complete-pack protection.

If the card carries a customer instruction, view it after the pack leaves the fixture but before the connection is removed. This is the moment the instruction may be needed. Record which face remains readable. A message hidden inside the fold should be assigned a later job or placed elsewhere, with the change kept in the card artwork revision.

Send the complete connection brief

product-hexagonal-folding-carton.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Hexagonal Folding Carton Sourcing

Specify a hexagonal folding carton with a six-panel plan and a formed view of both closures. Describe how the product sits inside the angled walls, including any holder. A single width or a photograph of a closed hexagon doesn't define the usable cavity or the opening sequence.

The angled shape is a structural choice, not only a visual theme. It changes where a product or holder meets the walls. Keep those contacts visible in the enquiry even if the outside artwork is still undecided.

Identify six walls in the formed position

The PakFactory hexagon catalogue confirms the named packaging direction. Ask for a proposed dieline and assembled drawing; its title alone doesn't establish your closure geometry, dimensions or contents arrangement.

Number the walls on a working plan and select the face intended to point forwards. Keep a note of the seam position relative to that front. If alternate panels carry artwork, check their order by folding a paper mock-up before completing the print file.

Use the existing foldable gift box collection to compare a rectangular format if the product needs a simpler cavity. A hexagonal outline earns its place when the internal arrangement and customer access are clear.

Show the product envelope against angled walls

For a round product, provide the maximum outside diameter and total packed height. Add any cap, tie or holder. For a non-round product, provide an oriented outline rather than trying to describe it with a circle.

A hypothetical round gift ornament might sit centrally in a paperboard holder. Show the holder's outer shape against the six walls and the product's position above it. A rectangular card tucked beside the ornament needs its own space and removal route.

Label internal across-flat and across-corner dimensions separately if the proposed drawing uses both. Let the supplier define allowances for the actual board and folds. Avoid converting one measurement into the other without confirming whether the drawing describes inside or outside geometry.

Make a cavity worksheet

Use the table for a specific drawing revision. Each row asks for a view or measurement that a general box-size field can miss.

AreaInput to provideCheck on the formed sample
Wall ringSix-wall plan and front faceWall sequence and seam position
Product outlineOriented packed envelopeClosest wall and corner contacts
BottomClosure drawing and forming orderBase complete before loading
TopOpening direction and gripClosure clears product and added card

The review should distinguish a round product that rotates from a holder that fixes one orientation. Choose which behavior you want; don't assume the shape settles that question.

Review forming, loading and removal in order

Confirm what arrives prepared, including the side seam and any bottom work. Form all six walls and the base before placing the holder. Photograph the empty cavity so a later fit issue can be compared with its unloaded geometry.

Load the complete product set, close the top and then open it as a customer would. Check whether fingers can reach the item without levering against a wall. Photograph any card that folds unexpectedly when the top closes.

Board, print, inserts and the outside shipping pack remain separate specification decisions. A six-wall sample review gives fit and action observations, not a verified transport result or maximum load.

If the product is intentionally oriented to one wall, name that wall on the cavity plan. Then review the top opening from the same front position. A round item may look similar after rotation, while a card or attachment does not. The panel map should carry that difference so the artwork, holder and loading instruction use one orientation.

product-hinged-metal-gift-container.post_title: Custom Hinged Metal Gift Container Sourcing
product-hinged-metal-gift-container.post_content:
Home / Jewelry Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Hinged Metal Gift Container Sourcing

A hinged metal gift container needs the attached lid’s travel and edge clearance reviewed with its insert. Identify the offered hinge axis, lid stop and rim detail, then check the actual gift’s removal route. The independent buying task is the moving metal closure, not a square or decorative tin shape.

The illustration is a dry, nonfood gift-pack concept. The actual metal, hinge, rim and holder proposal require project confirmation.

Bind the hinge to the offered container drawing

The original hinged-tin construction reference identifies attached-hinge metal containers. Request the offered drawing with the hinge axis, lid travel and edge details. Use that reference for mechanical identity; it does not establish a particular metal grade or the suitability of your contents.

Record the complete gift envelope, insert height and any card on or beneath the lid. Mark the point where the lid passes the holder and where its edge approaches the product. The open view and closed view should use the same arrangement.

Ask for the offered rim or edge construction rather than assuming every tin has the same rolled detail. State surfaces that should stay clear of contact with the product finish. A holder that fills the cavity can still need a different top clearance under the moving lid.

Review the hinge sweep through customer access

Load the actual gift, close the lid through its intended travel and reopen it using the proposed grip. Inspect the hinge-side and front-edge clearances before lifting the product. Record any holder movement, edge contact or card displacement at its location.

Compare the slip-lid metal gift container when a detached lid may suit the access route. The existing cardboard tube gift box also offers a different body/lid construction. Keep the product arrangement fixed while comparing the lid movement, edge and holder questions.

A packing change that lowers the insert or moves the care card should be retained as a revised configuration. The buyer should approve that complete arrangement rather than accepting the hinge alone while another component remains unresolved.

Use a hinge, edge and holder record

The hypothetical jewelry-gift table below records the interfaces without assigning seal or corrosion properties.

InterfaceExample inputSample question
Hinge H1Offered axis and travel/stop drawingWhat clearance remains behind the holder?
Front rim R1Offered metal edge detailWhere does the lid meet the closed pack?
Holder I1Jewelry primary pack and lift gripCan the gift be removed with the lid open?
Card C1Final position beside the lid sweepDoes the card move during closing?
Product finishNamed contact restrictionsWhat actual edge/contact is observed?

Give the proposal a complete open state

The container supplier should identify the hinge and rim construction. The holder converter should return the insert proposal at the same revision. The packing owner should show closing, opening and product removal using those parts. The buyer can then decide which interface needs a revision or additional sample review.

The sample revision method keeps a changed insert or lid detail attached to the accepted configuration. Bring the hinge drawing, complete gift and holder-clearance question to Get a Quote. MOQ is 500 pieces per design; material, sample scope and commercial terms are confirmed for the project.

product-hinged-nonmagnetic-rigid-box.post_content:
Home / Jewelry Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Ribbon-Tie Hinged Rigid Box Sourcing

A ribbon-tie hinged rigid box needs the ribbon to be defined as the closing action, with its anchors, route and release grip shown on the drawing. Review the tie around the loaded box so it clears the product and the moving cover. A decorative bow on another closure follows a different brief.

This concept explains a functional ribbon closure; the offered hinged structure, anchor details and material are confirmed for the project.

Identify what the tie actually closes

The rigid-box specification guide describes ribbon or paper-tie closures among rigid packaging choices. Ask the converter to show how the proposed tie joins the moving cover and base. Record the hinge/spine separately from the ribbon anchors.

State whether the ribbon passes through slits, is attached under a wrap or uses another offered construction. Give the free-end position, intended knot and customer grip as proposal fields. A drawing can then show which surfaces move and where the tie remains when the cover opens.

Add the product and insert height to the closing view. Include a card or accessory on the inside cover if one is planned. The ribbon can cross a different surface when untied, so inspect the open state as well as the closed bow.

Review tying and opening with the complete gift

Seat the gift in the holder, close the cover and tie it through the intended route. Open it again using the planned release grip. Photograph the anchor areas and the free ribbon ends beside the contents. Record any contact with the product finish, card or holder that needs a change.

Compare the existing magnetic jewelry box when its offered closure may better suit the project. The functional tie introduces an additional hand operation and customer release question. Keep that action explicit rather than treating the ribbon as a visual substitute for a hidden mechanism.

The collapsible gift-box direction also raises a separate supplied-state decision. If a rigid ribbon box arrives formed, record its storage and packout state rather than assuming it folds flat.

Use an anchor and tie-route record

This hypothetical jewelry-gift example defines the closing operation without assigning holding-force values.

Cover hingeSpine H1 on offered structureReview full cover travel
Ribbon anchorAttachment A1/A2 and wrap relationshipRequest attachment detail
Tie routeFront knot with free ends outside lid edgeReview loaded tying action
Open stateReleased ends stay clear of jewelry holderObserve finish/contact locations
Supplied stateFormed box and separate ribbon preparation if anyConfirm packing-owner action

Give the proposal a visible release route

The converter should identify anchor construction and the supplied ribbon/box state. The packing owner should retain the tying sequence and any positioning changes used in the sample. The buyer can then decide whether the tie is an acceptable closing action or whether another offered closure needs comparison.

Record the sample changes in the revision record so a relocated anchor stays connected to the box and wrap drawing.

Home / Inserts
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Hinged Thermoformed Clamshell Sourcing

A hinged thermoformed clamshell adds a moving lid and closing rim to the product cavity. Specify the hinge travel, closed internal height and customer release route with the complete gift component inside. Review the offered sheet and closure interface as one proposal instead of selecting a resin name before the geometry is clear.

The illustration is a nonfood gift-pack concept. The supplier confirms the actual formed sheet, hinge and rim engagement before sampling.

Separate the hinge from the closing interface

The original clamshell packaging reference distinguishes hinged and two-piece forms and describes several closing interfaces. Use that information to ask which mechanism the offered lid uses. A hinge connects the two halves; the rim or offered closing feature performs a separate action.

Request open and closed views of the same proposed pack. Mark the hinge axis, lid travel, cavity top and intended release grip. Include the actual product, primary wrap and insert card. The closed height must refer to that complete arrangement.

State whether the card sits behind the product, in the lid or against another surface. Locate its edge relative to the rim and hinge. A card can change a closing contact even when the product still sits correctly in the lower cavity.

Close and reopen around the real contents

Load the lower half, move the attached lid through its intended travel and pause before rim engagement. Inspect where the lid, card and product approach each other. Close using the offered method and reopen through the proposed customer grip.

Record any need to press directly on the product or to move a card before closure. Ask the converter for a located revision rather than adding that movement silently to the packing sequence. Retain the observed hinge and rim condition with the sample identity and agreed handling conditions.

Compare the open multi-cavity tray if a separate outer-box lid is preferable. The existing thermoformed insert direction is a broader holder choice; this clamshell specifically needs attached-lid travel and closed-rim access decisions.

Use a hinge and rim record

This hypothetical small gift-accessory pack separates the lid connection from its closure.

Rim R1Named engagement and release featureClosure detail on drawing

Card edgeProposed card position at lid travelLocated contact or clearance view

Give the converter a closed-pack question

The converter should confirm the formed geometry, closing interface and proposed sheet identity. The packing owner should report the actual loading and rim-engagement actions. The buyer should decide whether that customer access route is acceptable or whether a different lid/cavity proposal needs sampling.

product-hook-floor-gift-display.post_content:
Home / Foldable Gift Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Hook Floor Gift Display Sourcing

Specify a hook floor gift display with labeled hook rows, complete hanging-pack envelopes and an installation plan. Review customer removal in full and reduced stock states. A floor fixture needs its own layout and placement brief; it should not inherit the assumptions used for a small counter display.

This is a concept direction pending supplier confirmation of the body, base, hooks and joints. Required load or stability evidence belongs to a separate agreed evaluation.

Map actual hooks to actual hanging packs

The hook floor display reference names the direction. Request the proposed hook shape, length, attachment and row positions on front and side drawings. Include the base footprint and intended retail placement.

Provide each pack's hanging hole, complete outline and actual weight. Assign packs to hook IDs. An isolated hole fit does not show the pack's route past adjacent rows or a retaining end.

Compare a counter hook fixture when the placement is different. The useful distinction is the actual floor layout, setup and customer reach rather than a generic display name.

Review the loaded layout as stock changes

For a hypothetical display of small carded gifts, photograph the full hook arrangement before removal. Ask a reviewer to take a selected unit from the intended position without clearing neighbouring packs.

Repeat with the planned reduced stock. Record whether packs move forwards on a hook or staff rearrange them. Keep the customer's starting position and grip visible in the action record.

Review refill separately from customer removal. The hook's entry route can require another staff action, particularly when stock remains on nearby rows. Any unusual support or movement should be documented.

Use a floor-hook layout record

Keep each row's geometry and pack assignment together. The fixture's supplied state should match the installation instruction.

RecordRequired inputAction evidence
Hook identityShape, retaining end and attachmentActual pack placement
Row assignmentPack IDs, count and weightFull starting layout
Customer routeChosen unit and neighbouring stockRemoval without hidden clearing
Reduced/refill stateRemaining pattern and staff methodTwo separate action records
InstallationBody/base joins and placementSupplied-to-formed setup

Give a contact its hook, row and pack IDs. A general request for a wider fixture may miss a local relationship between two rows.

Confirm the installed proposal

In the hypothetical map, call one upper hook H1 and the pack directly below it BP1. If H1 removal meets BP1, record that relationship before changing the entire stand. Ask which hook position or pack assignment the supplier proposes to revise.

Confirm who installs the hooks and forms the base. Keep full and reduced layouts tied to the same complete fixture revision. Do not move the loaded fixture during a trial unless that is an agreed action with an appropriate scope.

The local record documents fit, reach and setup. It does not establish a rated load, universal accessibility or increased retail sales. Required evaluation should use the actual fixture and use conditions.

Custom Packaging Information Card Sourcing

Plan an informational card around the text the customer needs and the space it occupies inside the complete package.

Concept direction · Feasibility unverified

Your starting brief

Send the card’s finished and folded sizes, final copy, orientation and position in the pack. Identify who approves the text and how the customer will find, unfold and read it.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

Define content and occupied space

  • Provide final text and language versions with a named copy approver; separate unresolved copy from approved text.
  • State finished and folded size, the number and direction of folds, and the intended print sides.
  • Show where the card sits relative to the product, insert and lid, including the space needed for access.

Compare flat and folded information formats

Compare a flat card with a folded leaflet using the same copy and packing space. Choose by readable layout and customer access, then ask for the proposed stock and print specification. This component carries information; any structural support or protective function would need its own proposal and review.

If the card accompanies a candle gift, include it in the complete candle pack checklist rather than reviewing its size separately from the jar, insert and outer packaging.

Read the card in the complete pack

  • Proof the actual-size text, print sides and fold order against the approved copy version.
  • Load the card with the product and insert; check lid closure and the customer’s access to the information.
  • Keep the approved copy, artwork, card size and complete-pack sample versions together before requesting the final project scope.

MOQ and project scope

MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design. State the quantity for each design, not just the combined order total. Packrivo helps organize the brief and supplier questions. The relevant supplier confirms the proposed materials, construction, price, sample scope and delivery timing for the agreed configuration.

Include your destination and any open inputs. If a detail is not yet known, name who will provide it before the next review.

Before you send a brief

Can I use my own branding?

Include your desired logo placement, print surfaces and colors. Final artwork must use the approved supplier dieline and pass proof review.

Can you make exactly what the picture shows?

The picture is an AI-assisted concept, not a production promise. Structure, materials, tolerances and finishing need supplier review and a physical sample.

What happens after an inquiry?

A person reviews the brief and missing details. Supplier checks and sample or quotation discussions follow only after the next steps are agreed.

Home / Inserts
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Jewelry Mounting Card Sourcing

A jewelry mounting card uses holes, slots or another proposed attachment arrangement to present a piece on a printed card. Consider this direction when earrings, a necklace or a small set needs a defined display position inside a pouch, gift box or retail presentation. Plan the jewelry geometry, attachment and back of the card before choosing the front artwork.

Concept / inquiry direction. AI-assisted visuals explain the structure; final materials, production details and sample scope are agreed for the project.

Map the front and the back

The customer's view shows only part of the arrangement. Earring posts, backs, clasps and chain storage can project behind the card. Record those parts in the mounted position and identify what they may touch. A card that sits flat by itself can require additional depth when the jewelry is attached.

Describe each attachment point by its job: holding an earring pair level, routing a chain, retaining a pendant or leaving a removal route. Ask for the proposed hole or slot geometry against the actual piece. An attractive pattern of cuts is not enough to identify how the item is loaded or removed.

Keep hanging or retail-fixture holes separate from jewelry attachment points. One supports the presented pack on a fixture; the other positions the jewelry. Combining their purposes without a layout can change the visible orientation and make the back of the card difficult to access.

Reserve clear space around each attachment for the assembly action. Front artwork and back copy should be reviewed with the jewelry mounted.

Choose mounting rather than just information space

An information card carries instructions or brand copy. A mounting card adds an attachment and contact task, even when both are printed on similar material. A shaped box holder creates another set of loading and removal questions.

Decide whether the card travels in a pouch, rests in a box or hangs openly. That decision controls its outline, accessible edges and complete packed thickness. The jewelry measurement guide can help record posts, clasps and projections that the surrounding package must accommodate.

Prepare an attachment layout brief

FieldRecord for the proposed card
JewelryPiece count, geometry, weight, sensitive surfaces and mounted position.
AttachmentHole or slot locations, loading order, back fasteners and chain routing.
CardFinished outline, proposed material, folds and accessible removal edges.
Surrounding packPouch opening or box interior, complete thickness and packing sequence.
PrintFront and back copy, cutout positions and protected artwork areas.
ScopeQuantity by design, who mounts the jewelry and what the sample must answer.

For an illustrative necklace-and-earring set, the earrings may use front holes while the chain routes to the back. Show where the clasp sits and how the buyer releases the necklace. If a product variant changes those positions, review it as a mounted arrangement rather than substituting a photograph into the same artwork.

Review the mounted piece, then its package

  • Attach the actual jewelry using the proposed process.
  • Inspect position, contact surfaces and the back of the card.
  • Place the mounted card in its intended pouch or box.
  • Open the complete pack and take out the card by hand.
  • Remove the jewelry without making a new hole with the piece itself.
  • Record changes to the cuts, copy, material or surrounding pack.

The original jewelry display-card guide demonstrates why jewelry attachment needs deliberate holes and routing. Use its method discussion for context; supplier-specific cutting dimensions and production instructions still need to match your actual design.

Plan design quantities and mounting work

Packrivo's order planning policy is 500 pieces per product / design. Record different card artworks and attachment layouts as design questions, with the proposed mounting work and packaging components identified. Final material, pricing, production conditions and sample scope are agreed for the project.

Get a Quote with front and back views of the mounted layout and the removal you want. Packrivo helps connect the card, jewelry and surrounding pack before the sample review.

PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Kraft Bubble Parcel Envelope Sourcing

Specify a kraft bubble parcel envelope with separate records for the paper exterior, bubble lining and seam boundaries. Review the full product envelope against the inner contact surface and the closing method. A kraft-looking outside doesn't describe the complete material stack or the usable filled space.

This concept needs the actual layer materials and construction confirmed for the project. The category name is not a complete bill of materials.

Ask for the outer and inner component proposal

The kraft bubble mailer catalogue identifies the named direction. Request the exterior paper, lining material and any joining layers separately. Keep the product-contact material visible as a supplier question if it is not yet known.

Show seams and the opening in a section. Ask whether the lining continues into the flap area and which boundaries reduce usable space. A nominal outside width should not be copied into the interior record.

Compare a paper padded envelope through its confirmed layer proposal. Similar outside colors can sit over different inner interfaces, which should remain identified without a generic environmental claim.

Review fill, seam contact and closure

Provide the complete contents, packed orientation and highest point. Include any inner wrap that is intended between the product and lining. The source should know which surface it is being asked to assess.

For a hypothetical card-mounted gift accessory, review the backing-card corners at the mouth and along the seams. Load the full configuration before observing the closing flap. If an added wrap changes thickness, name that version separately.

The paper mailer brief supplies the wider project inputs. This direction adds an explicit two-material interface and its seam relationships.

Use a material-interface sheet

Keep supplier-confirmed composition separate from sample observations. Do not fill an unknown polymer or joining material from the picture.

Component/interfaceComponent specification for the quotationSample evidence
Outer paperGrade and print surfaceOutside loaded view
Bubble liningActual material and constructionContact-layer view
Paper to liningJoining proposal and extentSection or supplier explanation
Seam to contentsUsable internal boundariesLocated entry/contact image
Closing regionFlap and receiving surfaceLoaded closing route

If the supplier replaces a layer, record the changed component and request the relevant new evidence. The envelope name can remain the same while the contact or closing interface changes.

Keep the review question located

In the hypothetical record, call the lining IL1 and the card corner CC1. A question about CC1 entering beside a seam is different from one about the product resting on IL1. Keep separate observations if both occur.

Confirm the supplied preparation and packing responsibility. State how the parcel is labeled and where the intended customer opening begins. Required handling or distribution performance needs a separate complete-system evaluation.

Inspect the inner contact surface and contents after removal within the agreed sample scope. Record what is visible without claiming barrier, recyclability, cushioning or food suitability from the layer names alone.

Send the complete component stack

product-latch-metal-gift-container.post_title: Custom Latch Metal Gift Container Sourcing
product-latch-metal-gift-container.post_content:
Home / Jewelry Boxes
PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Latch Metal Gift Container Sourcing

Specify a latch metal gift container by the release point, proposed lid movement and complete inner pack. Review the hand action with contents loaded, then inspect the finished contact areas. Request the latch mechanism and attachment details separately from any security, sealing or performance requirement.

This enquiry concept is for dry gifts. The actual metal, lining, edge construction and latch/lid arrangement need supplier confirmation.

Identify the latch and lid proposal

The latch tin catalogue identifies the closure direction. Request the actual latch parts and their attachment to the lid and body. Show whether a hinge or another lid movement is proposed; the name alone doesn't settle that detail.

Mark the release point and hand route. Keep the external hardware separate from inner lining or covering layers. Ask which components arrive assembled and how paired parts are identified.

Compare a screw-top direction if a rotating lid is another option. The meaningful difference is the actual closing and opening action around the same dry gift.

Review the full inner pack

Provide the product, holder, pouch and card envelope. Mark any part near the latch, rim or proposed hinge. Record the actual finished contact surface from the supplier proposal.

For a hypothetical gift accessory in an inner pouch, close the loaded container before reviewing latch release. Keep the pouch position fixed. A pouch moved away from the rim for the opening photograph describes another configuration.

After release, follow the confirmed lid route and remove the contents. Record any hand or product contact by location. Finished-edge and use requirements should be given to the responsible supplier without asserting a universal safety result.

Use a latch interaction map

Keep one paired lid/body and hardware revision throughout the sequence. The map separates release, lid travel and product access.

Action/interfaceHardware or interface in the supplier proposalEvidence
Latch releaseHardware and finger routeClosed loaded starting view
Latch engagementConfirmed final relationshipLoaded closing view
Lid travelHinge or movement proposalOpening arc around contents
Edge/contactFinished surfaces and inner packLocated hand/product observation
Product removalHolder or pouch routeOpened complete configuration

Use the sample revision record to keep paired components and any changed hardware traceable. A familiar container color does not identify the same latch construction.

Ask a located release question

In the hypothetical map, call the latch LT1 and pouch edge PE1. If PE1 sits near the release route, record both parts before asking for a revised container size. The source can assess the actual interference.

If a proposal changes the hardware, lid movement or lining, retain those component changes and repeat the relevant action. Outside artwork approval can remain a separate decision from the latch interface.

Any retention, security, repeated-use or distribution requirement needs defined responsible evidence. The local action record doesn't establish those results or adopt the catalogue's food-use claim.

Submit the loaded latch brief

Custom Lightweight Mailer Box Sourcing

MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design. Plan the quantity for each design in your brief.

Describe a mailer for a defined packed product and handling route; treat the proposed box weight as a comparison input, not proof of protection.

Concept direction · Feasibility unverified

Your starting brief

Send the complete packed product dimensions and weight, destination, delivery route and proposed closure. Identify any insert or wrap that will be used so suppliers compare the same packing system.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

Describe the complete packed product

  • Measure and weigh the item with its retail packaging, wrap, cards and other shipped contents.
  • Identify protruding or delicate parts, surfaces that should not rub, and the loading and removal sequence.
  • State the proposed mailer interior, closure, delivery format and destination; record unknowns rather than guessing a board specification.

Compare the whole pack before its weight

Compare a mailer with a fitted insert, a compartment layout and an alternative outer box using the same contents. Ask each supplier to identify the proposed construction and its basis. A lower box weight is useful information for comparison, but the packed system still needs an agreed sample and handling review.

For a mailer that needs an insert, the mailer and insert fit brief shows which product measurements and loading details to collect before requesting a candidate.

Review closure, movement and access

  • Load the actual product and all packing components; check whether the closure seats as intended.
  • Use the agreed handling or transport evaluation for the defined pack and route, with an owner and recorded acceptance method.
  • Record product movement, contact points and the opening experience. Keep observations tied to the tested box, insert and closure versions.

MOQ and project scope

MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design. State the quantity for each design, not just the combined order total. Packrivo helps organize the brief and supplier questions. The relevant supplier confirms the proposed materials, construction, price, sample scope and delivery timing for the agreed configuration.

Include your destination and any open inputs. If a detail is not yet known, name who will provide it before the next review.

Can I use my own branding?

Include your desired logo placement, print surfaces and colors. Final artwork must use the approved supplier dieline and pass proof review.

Can you make exactly what the picture shows?

The picture is an AI-assisted concept, not a production promise. Structure, materials, tolerances and finishing need supplier review and a physical sample.

What happens after an inquiry?

A person reviews the brief and missing details. Supplier checks and sample or quotation discussions follow only after the next steps are agreed.

PACKAGING DIRECTION

Custom Lock-Cap Auto-Bottom Carton Sourcing

Specify a lock-cap auto-bottom carton by drawing the upper cap engagement and the prepared bottom separately. The bottom forms the loading base; the cap closes against a receiving feature above the contents. Review the cap with the insert, care card and product already in place so the closing and opening routes remain usable.

This concept direction uses an offered cap and base drawing; the supplier confirms the actual tabs, receivers and material.

Give the top cap its own interface

The lock-cap auto-bottom catalogue supports the named construction. Ask the converter to point to the cap tab and the matching receiver on the proposed blank. A lock name does not tell your packing team where to press, which panel moves first or how the customer releases it.

Show the carton both open and fully closed. On the open view, mark the final contents height, the cap sweep and any inside panel or slot receiving the lock. On the closed view, mark the grip used to release the cap. Keep a printed front label separate from those mechanical identities.

A care card can become part of the top-contact question. State whether it lies flat over the product, stands behind it or sits in a separate holder. Include its final folded size rather than only its artwork dimensions. The cap should be reviewed against the complete arrangement, not against an empty cavity.

Form the base before testing the cap

The auto-bottom carton focuses on prepared-base erection. The full-flap auto-bottom direction adds a base coverage question. This lock-cap direction adds upper engagement and customer release; record those as different actions instead of treating every automatic-bottom name as the same choice.

Have the packing owner form the bottom using the offered instructions and load the contents. Stop just before cap engagement and photograph the upper clearance. Then close and reopen using the intended grip. If a tab presses against the card or requires moving the product, locate that contact and ask for a drawing-based change. Do not hide the adjustment inside an informal packing habit.

Keep a cap and base action table

For a hypothetical jewelry gift carton, the following record separates the empty setup from the loaded closing step.

ActionBrief entryWho confirms it
Base erectionPrepared joint/base folds on drawing BX1Converter and packing owner
Contents heightJewelry holder plus the care card in its final positionBuyer supplies the complete set
Cap engagementTab T1 enters receiver R1 on offered drawingConverter identifies the mechanism
Customer releaseNamed grip and opening movementBuyer reviews loaded sample
Card contactRecord any contact before changing the card positionPacking owner returns located evidence

Make the closure decision reviewable

The converter’s next response should identify the tab, receiver and cap clearance, not simply confirm that a lock cap is available. The packing owner’s response should describe the sequence used with the actual contents. Your approval should reference both, with the sample and drawing revision named.

Read the general tuck-end carton direction if a simple tuck closure is also being considered. Use the delivery-state record to keep factory preparation and local packing actions clear.

Custom Mailer Box with Fitted Insert Sourcing

A mailer and fitted insert should be briefed as one coordinated system.

Inquiry direction · Supplier confirmation required

Quote Details

Send the product dimensions, quantity by design and destination. Include the structure, material and artwork preferences you already know; flag open questions so supplier quotes use the same scope.

Get a QuoteExplore customization →

When it may fit

It may suit a set that needs separate positions inside a parcel. It may not fit a product assortment whose dimensions change frequently without variant-specific layouts.

Details to define

  • Product sizes, weights, count and orientation.
  • Insert layout, cavity dimensions and removal access.
  • Box interior, insert material preference, artwork and pack sequence.
  • Quantity, destination and sample review conditions.

Artwork and presentation choices

Coordinate the mailer artwork with the insert layout. Give each cavity a content reference and keep the printed information card distinct from the product-holding component.

Options to compare

  • Compare a single cavity with a multi-item layout.
  • Consider contrasting colors across the outer mailer and inner insert.
  • Decide what visual moment matters when the lid opens.

Supplier confirmation needed

Confirm material, tolerances, box compatibility and sample contents. The insert image does not prove protection or fit for different product variants.

Project details to agree

Final materials, construction, price, sample scope and delivery timing are confirmed for the agreed project with the relevant supplier.

Quote inputs to prepare

  • Actual product size and packed weight, including any accessories.
  • Inner cavity and insert layout, with estimated and measured dimensions separated.
  • Outer mailer size, board and printing preferences, and packing state.
  • Expected quantity, variant split and destination country.

What to approve on a sample

  • Product retention and removal in the fitted insert.
  • Closure, fold lines and the final assembled dimensions.
  • Protection checks appropriate to the packed product and shipping route.
  • Approved artwork, insert layout and packed carton specification.

Move this packaging project forward

Packrivo helps turn this direction into a clear brief, coordinate supplier questions, compare responses and review sample evidence against your product.

Use the quote comparison checklist to keep the mailer and insert in the same quoted scope.

Plan the quotation and sample scope

Request the box or pouch, insert where needed, decoration, sampling, packing and delivery as separate cost items. Confirm the quoted specification, quantity, currency, trade terms and validity before comparing offers. MOQ: 500 pieces per product / design.

Agree what a structural sample will check and which printed or finished sample is needed before production approval. Record the specification and sample version so a later change does not silently replace an earlier approval.

Keep market references separate from supplier confirmation and a project quotation. Use the quotation comparison checklist and sample approval checklist before approving the next step.

Frequently asked questions

Should box and insert be requested together?

Yes. Share the packed product layout and ask the supplier to review the box and insert as one system.

Is the material or use claim confirmed?

No. This is an inquiry candidate. Exact composition, market suitability, supplier feasibility, project price and timing and performance need evidence.
